The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Two-Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
summary: Grab a dumbbell with each arm and place the upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbell should be held at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
steps: Grab a dumbbell with each arm and place the upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbell should be held at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weights up until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height.
Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Zottman Preacher Curl
summary: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and place your upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbells should be held at shoulder height and the elbows should be flexed. Hold the dumbbells with the palms of your hands facing down. This will be your starting position.
steps: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and place your upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbells should be held at shoulder height and the elbows should be flexed. Hold the dumbbells with the palms of your hands facing down. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells keeping the palms down until your upper arm is extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
Now rotate your wrists once you are at the bottom of the movement so that the palms of the hands are facing up.

As you exhale, use your biceps to curl the weights up until they are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height. Again, remember that to ensure full contraction you need to bring that small finger higher than the thumb.
Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and rotate your wrists so that the palms are facing down again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Heavy Bag Thrust
summary: Utilize a heavy bag for this exercise. Assume an upright stance next to the bag, with your feet staggered, fairly wide apart. Place your hand on the bag at about chest height. This will be your starting position.
steps: Utilize a heavy bag for this exercise. Assume an upright stance next to the bag, with your feet staggered, fairly wide apart. Place your hand on the bag at about chest height. This will be your starting position.
Begin by twisting at the waist, pushing the bag forward as hard as possible. Perform this move quickly, pushing the bag away from your body.
Receive the bag as it swings back by reversing these steps.

title: Back Flyes - With Bands
summary: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
steps: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises.

Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides.
After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Box Squat with Bands
summary: Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you. Set up the bands on the sleeves, secured to either band pegs, the rack, or dumbbells so that there is appropriate tension. If dumbbells are used, secure them so that they don't move. Also, ensure that the dumbbells you are using are heavy enough for the bands that you are using. Additional plates can be used to hold the dumbbells down. If more tension is needed, you can either widen the base on the floor or choke the bands. Typically, you would aim for a box height that brings you to a parallel squat, but you can train higher or lower if desired.
steps: Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you. Set up the bands on the sleeves, secured to either band pegs, the rack, or dumbbells so that there is appropriate tension. If dumbbells are used, secure them so that they don't move. Also, ensure that the dumbbells you are using are heavy enough for the bands that you are using. Additional plates can be used to hold the dumbbells down. If more tension is needed, you can either widen the base on the floor or choke the bands. Typically, you would aim for a box height that brings you to a parallel squat, but you can train higher or lower if desired.

Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wider for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, or closer together for more quad development. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips until you are seated on the box. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Pause when you reach the box, and relax the hip flexors. Never bounce off of a box.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward off of the box as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe. Use care to return the barbell to the rack.

title: Calf Raises - With Bands
summary: Grab an exercise band and stand on it with your toes making sure that the length of the band between the foot and the arms is the same for both sides.
steps: Grab an exercise band and stand on it with your toes making sure that the length of the band between the foot and the arms is the same for both sides.

While holding the handles of the band, raise the arms to the side of your head as if you were getting ready to perform a shoulder press. The palms should be facing forward with the elbows bent and to the sides. This movement will create tension on the band. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the hands by your shoulder, stand up on your toes as you exhale and contract the calves hard at the top of the movement.
After a one second contraction, slowly go back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Cross Over - With Bands
summary: Secure an exercise band around a stationary post.
steps: Secure an exercise band around a stationary post.
While facing away from the post, grab the handles on both ends of the band and step forward enough to create tension on the band.

Raise your arms to the sides, parallel to the floor, perpendicular to your torso (your torso and the arms should resemble the letter "T") and with the palms facing forward. Have them extended with a slight bend at the elbows. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your arms straight, bring them across your chest in a semicircular motion to the front as you exhale and flex your pecs. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position as you inhale.
Perform for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Deadlift with Bands
summary: To deadlift with short bands, simply loop them over the bar before you start, and step into them to set up. For long bands, they will need to be anchored to a secure base, such as heavy dumbbells or a rack.
steps: To deadlift with short bands, simply loop them over the bar before you start, and step into them to set up. For long bands, they will need to be anchored to a secure base, such as heavy dumbbells or a rack.

With your feet, and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and bend the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
tips: 1. Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping
2. Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower back down
3. Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form

title: Hip Extension with Bands
summary: Secure one end of the band to the lower portion of a post and attach the other to one ankle.
steps: Secure one end of the band to the lower portion of a post and attach the other to one ankle.
Facing the attachment point of the band, hold on to the column to stabilize yourself.
Keeping your head and your chest up, move the resisted leg back as far as you can while keeping the knee straight.
Return the leg to the starting position.

title: Upright Cable Row
summary: Grasp a straight bar cable attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The bar should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.
steps: Grasp a straight bar cable attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The bar should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the cable bar as you exhale. The bar should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until it nearly touches your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the bar, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Shoulder Press
summary: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack. Position a barbell at a height that is just above your head. Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward).
steps: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack. Position a barbell at a height that is just above your head. Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward).

Once you pick up the barbell with the correct grip width, lift the bar up over your head by locking your arms. Hold at about shoulder level and slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Lower the bar down to the shoulders slowly as you inhale.
Lift the bar back up to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Shoulder Press
summary: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight.
steps: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight.
Stand directly in between the uprights. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press the handles directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat.

title: Dumbbell One-Arm Shoulder Press
summary: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight.
steps: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight.
Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface.
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch arms.

title: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
summary: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, sit on a military press bench or utility bench that has back support. Place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs.
steps: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, sit on a military press bench or utility bench that has back support. Place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs.
Now raise the dumbbells to shoulder height one at a time using your thighs to help propel them up into position.
Make sure to rotate your wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. This is your starting position.
Now, exhale and push the dumbbells upward until they touch at the top.
Then, after a brief pause at the top contracted position, slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Leverage Shoulder Press
summary: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height. The handles should be near the top of the shoulders at the beginning of the motion. Your chest and head should be up and handles held with a pronated grip. This will be your starting position.
steps: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height. The handles should be near the top of the shoulders at the beginning of the motion. Your chest and head should be up and handles held with a pronated grip. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles upward by extending through the elbow.
After a brief pause at the top, return the weight to just above the start position, keeping tension on the muscles by not returning the weight to the stops until the set is complete.

title: Machine Shoulder (Military) Press
summary: Sit down on the Shoulder Press Machine and select the weight.
steps: Sit down on the Shoulder Press Machine and select the weight.
Grab the handles to your sides as you keep the elbows bent and in line with your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now lift the handles as you exhale and you extend the arms fully. At the top of the position make sure that you hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the handles slowly back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Decline Smith Press
summary: Place a decline bench underneath the Smith machine. Now place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Using a pronated grip that is wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Place a decline bench underneath the Smith machine. Now place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Using a pronated grip that is wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, lower the bar under control by allowing the elbows to flex, lightly contacting the torso.
After a brief pause, bring the bar back to the starting position by extending the elbows, exhaling as you do so.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When the set is complete, lock the bar back in the rack.

title: Smith Incline Shoulder Raise
summary: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the incline bench and make sure your shoulders are aligned right under the barbell.
steps: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the incline bench and make sure your shoulders are aligned right under the barbell.
Using a shoulder width pronated (palms forward) grip, lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with a slight bend at the elbows. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe out, lift the bar up until your arms are fully extended. Note: The contraction should be felt around the shoulders.
After a second pause, bring the bar back down to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

title: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug
summary: With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.
steps: With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.

Stand with the bar behind you, taking a shoulder-width, pronated grip on the bar and unhook the weight. You should be standing up straight with your head and chest up and your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by shrugging your shoulders straight up. Do not flex the arms or wrist during the movement.
After a brief pause return the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.

title: Smith Machine Bench Press
summary: Place a flat bench underneath the smith machine. Now place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the flat bench. Using a pronated grip that is wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
steps: Place a flat bench underneath the smith machine. Now place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the flat bench. Using a pronated grip that is wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, lock the bar back in the rack.

title: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
summary: Set the barbell attached to the smith machine to a height that is about 2 inches below your knees.
steps: Set the barbell attached to the smith machine to a height that is about 2 inches below your knees.
Bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up.

Now grasp the barbell using an overhand (pronated) grip and unlock it from the smith machine rack. Then let it hang directly in front of you as your arms hang extended perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.

While keeping the torso stationary, lift the barbell as you breathe out, keeping the elbows close to the body and not doing any force with the forearm other than holding the weights. On the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the weight again to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Smith Machine Calf Raise
summary: Place a block or weight plate below the bar on the Smith machine. Set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step onto the plates with the balls of your feet and place the bar on the back of your shoulders.
steps: Place a block or weight plate below the bar on the Smith machine. Set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step onto the plates with the balls of your feet and place the bar on the back of your shoulders.
Take the bar with both hands facing forward. Rotate the bar to unrack it. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as high as possible by pushing off of the balls of your feet, flexing your calf at the top of the contraction. Your knees should remain extended. Hold the contracted position for a second before you start to go back down.
Return slowly to the starting position as you breathe in while lowering your heels.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your heels and inhaling as you lower them back down
2. Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk
3. Ensure your knees remain slightly bent to avoid knee strain

title: Rack Delivery
summary: This drill teaches the delivery of the barbell to the rack position on the shoulders. Begin holding a bar in the scarecrow position, with the upper arms parallel to the floor, and the forearms hanging down. Use a hook grip, with your fingers wrapped over your thumbs.
steps: This drill teaches the delivery of the barbell to the rack position on the shoulders. Begin holding a bar in the scarecrow position, with the upper arms parallel to the floor, and the forearms hanging down. Use a hook grip, with your fingers wrapped over your thumbs.

Begin by rotating the elbows around the bar, delivering the bar to the shoulders. As your elbows come forward, relax your grip. The shoulders should be protracted, providing a shelf for the bar, which should lightly contact the throat.

It is important that the bar stay close to the body at all times, as with a heavier load any distance will result in an unwanted collision. As the movement becomes smoother, speed and load can be increased before progressing further.

title: Rack Pulls
summary: Set up in a power rack with the bar on the pins. The pins should be set to the desired point; just below the knees, just above, or in the mid thigh position. Position yourself against the bar in proper deadlifting position. Your feet should be under your hips, your grip shoulder width, back arched, and hips back to engage the hamstrings. Since the weight is typically heavy, you may use a mixed grip, a hook grip, or use straps to aid in holding the weight.
steps: Set up in a power rack with the bar on the pins. The pins should be set to the desired point; just below the knees, just above, or in the mid thigh position. Position yourself against the bar in proper deadlifting position. Your feet should be under your hips, your grip shoulder width, back arched, and hips back to engage the hamstrings. Since the weight is typically heavy, you may use a mixed grip, a hook grip, or use straps to aid in holding the weight.
With your head looking forward, extend through the hips and knees, pulling the weight up and back until lockout. Be sure to pull your shoulders back as you complete the movement.
Return the weight to the pins and repeat.

title: T-Bar Row with Handle
summary: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end.
steps: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end.
Stand over the bar, and position a Double D row handle around the bar next to the collar. Using your hips and legs, rise to a standing position.
Assume a wide stance with your hips back and your chest up. Your arms should be extended. This will be your starting position.
Pull the weight to your upper abdomen by retracting the shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Do not jerk the weight or cheat during the movement.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

title: Dip Machine
summary: Sit securely in a dip machine, select the weight and firmly grasp the handles.
steps: Sit securely in a dip machine, select the weight and firmly grasp the handles.
Now keep your elbows in at your sides in order to place emphasis on the triceps. The elbows should be bent at a 90 degree angle.
As you contract the triceps, extend your arms downwards as you exhale. Tip: At the bottom of the movement, focus on keeping a little bend in your arms to keep tension on the triceps muscle.
Now slowly let your arms come back up to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Triceps Extension
summary: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position.
steps: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by extending the elbow, pulling your lower arm away from your upper arm.
Pause at the completion of the movement, and then slowly return the weight to the starting position.
Avoid returning the weight all the way to the stops until the set is complete to keep tension on the muscles being worked.

title: Elliptical Trainer
summary: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.
steps: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.
Set the resistance and start moving - your feet trace a long oval and never leave the pedals.
Keep your torso upright rather than leaning on the handles.

title: Stairmaster
summary: Step onto the stairs and hold the rails without putting weight on them.
steps: Step onto the stairs and hold the rails without putting weight on them.
Set the pace and climb, straightening the leg fully at the top.
Stay upright instead of hunching over the console.

title: Step Mill
summary: Step onto the moving stairs and hold the rails for balance.
steps: Step onto the moving stairs and hold the rails for balance.
Climb at the set pace, placing the whole foot on each step.
Do not lean your weight on the rails - it takes the work off your legs.

title: Bicycling, Stationary
summary: Set the saddle so your leg is almost straight at the bottom.
steps: Set the saddle so your leg is almost straight at the bottom.
Set the resistance and pedal at an even pace.
Keep your back neutral instead of collapsing onto the bars.

title: Recumbent Bike
summary: Sit back against the rest and set the distance to the pedals.
steps: Sit back against the rest and set the distance to the pedals.
Pedal at an even pace with a resistance you can hold.
Leave a small bend in the knee at full extension.

title: Battling Ropes
summary: Take an end in each hand, stand in a quarter squat, feet hip width.
steps: Take an end in each hand, stand in a quarter squat, feet hip width.
Raise and drop the arms alternately to send waves down the ropes.
Work with the whole body rather than only the arms; keep the back flat.

title: Rope Climb
summary: Grip the rope as high as you can reach and clamp it between your feet.
steps: Grip the rope as high as you can reach and clamp it between your feet.
Pull up, tuck the knees, re-clamp higher and stand through the legs.
Come down under control, hand over hand, rather than sliding.

title: Pullups
summary: Take an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders and hang.
steps: Take an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders and hang.
Pull the shoulder blades down and together until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to straight arms.

title: Chin-Up
summary: Take an underhand grip at shoulder width and hang.
steps: Take an underhand grip at shoulder width and hang.
Pull with the elbows driving down and back until the chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly rather than dropping.
tips: 1. Focus on using your biceps and back muscles to lift your body, avoiding excessive momentum
2. Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury
3. Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain
4. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself
5. Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your chin above the bar at the top

title: Muscle Up
summary: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip and build a small swing.
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip and build a small swing.
Pull hard and drive the chest over the bar, rolling the wrists over.
Press to straight arms, then reverse the path down.

title: One Arm Chin-Up
summary: Take the bar with one hand and tuck the other behind your back.
steps: Take the bar with one hand and tuck the other behind your back.
Pull until the chin clears the bar without letting the torso rotate.
Lower under control, then match the reps on the other arm.

title: Scapular Pull-Up
summary: Hang from the bar with straight arms and relaxed shoulders.
steps: Hang from the bar with straight arms and relaxed shoulders.
Without bending the arms, pull the shoulder blades down and together.
Return to a free hang. The movement is short and comes only from the shoulder blades.

title: Kipping Muscle Up
summary: Hang from the bar and set up a pendulum with the whole body.
steps: Hang from the bar and set up a pendulum with the whole body.
On the forward swing pull hard and drive the chest over the bar.
Press to straight arms, then come down and damp the swing.

title: Hanging Leg Raise
summary: Hang from a bar or brace on the parallel bars with the torso still.
steps: Hang from a bar or brace on the parallel bars with the torso still.
Raise straight legs to horizontal by curling the pelvis upward.
Lower slowly without swinging.

title: Hanging Pike
summary: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip.
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip.
Raise straight legs toward the bar, folding at the hips.
Lower under control to a full hang.

title: Russian Twist
summary: Sit with the knees bent and lean back to about forty-five degrees.
steps: Sit with the knees bent and lean back to about forty-five degrees.
Rotate the torso left and right, letting the hands follow.
Keep the back flat - the rotation comes from the torso, not the arms.
tips: 1. Move your torso, not just your arms, to ensure you are engaging your oblique muscles
2. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you rotate to each side and inhaling as you return to the center
3. Keep your back straight and avoid hunching your shoulders to maintain proper form

title: Cable Russian Twists
summary: Sit side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in both hands.
steps: Sit side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in both hands.
Lean back and rotate the torso away from the pulley and back.
Move the hands with the torso, keeping them on the line of the chest.

title: Seated Barbell Twist
summary: Sit on a bench with the bar across your shoulders and feet flat.
steps: Sit on a bench with the bar across your shoulders and feet flat.
Rotate the torso left and right through a comfortable range.
Keep the hips still - the movement belongs to the upper back.
tips: 1. Engage your core muscles to stabilize your spine and maintain proper form
2. Maintain an upright posture to avoid straining your lower back
3. Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury

title: Front Plate Raise
summary: Hold a plate by its edges with both hands, arms down in front.
steps: Hold a plate by its edges with both hands, arms down in front.
Raise the plate to eye level with straight arms.
Lower slowly without help from the torso.
tips: 1. Avoid using momentum to lift the plate; focus on a slow and controlled movement
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints
3. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the plate and inhaling as you lower it

title: Plate Pinch
summary: Hold two plates smooth sides out and pinch them with the fingers.
steps: Hold two plates smooth sides out and pinch them with the fingers.
Hold them at your side for as long as you can.
Set the plates down under control rather than dropping them.

title: Plate Twist
summary: Sit with the knees bent and hold a plate in both hands at the chest.
steps: Sit with the knees bent and hold a plate in both hands at the chest.
Lean back and rotate the torso with the plate left and right.
Keep the back flat and the movement smooth.

title: Reverse Plate Curls
summary: Hold a plate by its edges with both hands, arms hanging down.
steps: Hold a plate by its edges with both hands, arms hanging down.
Bend the elbows to bring the plate to chest height, upper arms still.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

title: Air Bike Intervals
summary: Set the seat so your leg is almost straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
steps: Set the seat so your leg is almost straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up for three minutes at an easy pace, using both arms and legs.
Work hard for 20 seconds, then pedal easily for 90 seconds. Repeat six times.
Finish with two minutes of easy pedalling.

title: Air Bike Steady Effort
summary: Sit tall, shoulders relaxed, hands on the moving handles.
steps: Sit tall, shoulders relaxed, hands on the moving handles.
Pedal at a pace you could hold a conversation at for fifteen minutes.
Keep the effort even — the fan gets harder the faster you go, so do not start too fast.

title: Ski Erg Intervals
summary: Stand tall, grip the handles above your head, feet under your hips.
steps: Stand tall, grip the handles above your head, feet under your hips.
Hinge at the hips and pull the handles down past your thighs, finishing with straight arms.
Stand back up and reset. Work for 30 seconds, rest for 60, repeat eight times.

title: Ski Erg Steady Pull
summary: Grip the handles overhead with a tall spine and soft knees.
steps: Grip the handles overhead with a tall spine and soft knees.
Drive the handles down using your lats and your body weight, not just your arms.
Return smoothly to the top and continue at an even pace for ten minutes.

title: 45-Degree Bicycle Twisting Crunch
summary: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and lift both feet off the floor, knees bent to a right angle.
steps: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and lift both feet off the floor, knees bent to a right angle.
Curl the head and shoulders off the floor and press the lower back down. This is the starting position.
Extend one leg out to about 45 degrees while drawing the opposite knee in, and rotate your torso so that shoulder turns toward the bent knee.
Switch sides in one smooth movement, turning from the ribs rather than pulling on your neck.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then lower the head and feet together.
tips: 1. Ensure your feet are securely positioned on the hyperextension bench to maintain stability throughout the exercise
2. Focus on engaging your core muscles to lift and twist, avoiding pulling on your neck with your hands
3. Perform the exercise with controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and reduce the risk of strain

title: 45-Degree Side Bend
summary: Set a 45-degree back extension bench and climb on sideways, so one hip rests on the pad and your feet are locked under the rollers.
steps: Set a 45-degree back extension bench and climb on sideways, so one hip rests on the pad and your feet are locked under the rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head and hold the torso in line with the legs. This is the starting position.
Bend sideways toward the floor as you breathe in, letting the top side of your waist lengthen.
Raise the torso back up until it is in line with the legs as you breathe out, and squeeze the side of the waist for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then turn over and work the other side.
tips: 1. Maintain a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and prevent strain
2. Focus on using your oblique muscles to lift your upper body, avoiding any jerking or sudden movements
3. Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it during the exercise

title: Air Twisting Crunch
summary: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and raise both legs so the hips and knees are bent to right angles.
steps: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and raise both legs so the hips and knees are bent to right angles.
Curl the head and shoulders off the floor and keep the lower back pressed down. This is the starting position.
Rotate the torso so one shoulder travels toward the opposite knee as you breathe out, keeping both feet in the air.
Return to the middle as you breathe in, then repeat to the other side.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions without letting the feet touch the floor.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maximize muscle activation and protect your lower back
2. Perform the movement slowly and with control, avoiding the use of momentum to maximize effectiveness
3. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you twist and bring your elbow to your knee, and inhaling as you switch sides

title: Band Decline Sit-Up
summary: Start out by strapping the bands around the base of the decline bench. Place the handles towards the inside of the decline bench so that when lying down, you can reach for both of them.
steps: Start out by strapping the bands around the base of the decline bench. Place the handles towards the inside of the decline bench so that when lying down, you can reach for both of them.

Position your legs through the decline machine until they are secured. Now reach for the exercise bands with both hands. Use a pronated (palms forward) grip to grasp the handles. Position them near your collar bone and rotate your wrist to a neutral grip (palms facing the torso). Note: Your arms should remain stationary throughout the exercise. This is the starting position.

Move your torso upward until your upper body is perpendicular to the floor while exhaling. Hold the contraction for a second and lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored behind the headrest to avoid slipping
2. Exhale as you lift your upper body and inhale as you lower it back down
3. Avoid pulling on the band with your arms; focus on using your abs to lift your body

title: Band Side Bend
summary: Stand on one end of a resistance band with the foot on the same side as the working hand and hold the other end at your side.
steps: Stand on one end of a resistance band with the foot on the same side as the working hand and hold the other end at your side.
Stand tall with the feet hip width apart, the free hand behind your head and the band already under tension. This is the starting position.
Bend sideways away from the anchored foot as you breathe in, letting the band lengthen along your working side.
Pull yourself back upright with the side of your waist as you breathe out, and hold for a second at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then change sides.
tips: 1. Engage your core to help stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement
2. Avoid bending forward or backward; focus on bending directly to the side
3. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you bend to the side and inhaling as you return to the upright position

title: Band Standing Crunch
summary: Anchor a resistance band above head height and stand facing away from it, holding an end in each hand beside your ears.
steps: Anchor a resistance band above head height and stand facing away from it, holding an end in each hand beside your ears.
Step forward until the band is under tension, feet hip width apart and knees soft. This is the starting position.
Crunch the ribs down toward your hips as you breathe out, rounding the upper back rather than folding at the hips.
Let the band draw you back upright slowly as you breathe in, keeping the hands beside your ears throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Band Standing Lift
summary: Anchor a resistance band at floor level and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands beside the hip nearest the anchor.
steps: Anchor a resistance band at floor level and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands beside the hip nearest the anchor.
Step out until the band is under tension, feet shoulder width apart and knees slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Pull the hands up and diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder as you breathe out, rotating through the hips and turning the back foot.
Return along the same diagonal slowly as you breathe in, letting the band lower you rather than dropping.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then change sides.

title: Band Standing Twist
summary: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands with the arms straight out in front of your chest.
steps: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands with the arms straight out in front of your chest.
Step out until the band is under tension, feet shoulder width apart and the core braced. This is the starting position.
Rotate the torso away from the anchor, keeping the arms straight and the hips facing forward, until the band is fully loaded.
Return to the middle slowly as you breathe in, resisting the pull rather than letting it snap you back.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then turn around and work the other side.

title: Band Twist - Up and Down
summary: Anchor a resistance band high on one side and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands above the near shoulder with the arms straight.
steps: Anchor a resistance band high on one side and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in both hands above the near shoulder with the arms straight.
Step out until the band is under tension and set the feet shoulder width apart. This is the starting position.
Pull the hands down and diagonally across your body toward the opposite hip as you breathe out, turning the ribs and pivoting the back foot.
Reverse the path slowly back up above the shoulder as you breathe in, keeping the arms straight throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then change sides.

title: Bent Knee Lying Twist
summary: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and the knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and the knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
Press both shoulder blades into the floor. This is the starting position.
Let both knees fall together to one side, keeping the shoulders down, until you feel the stretch through the lower back and waist.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then bring the knees back to the middle and repeat to the other side.
tips: 1. Keep your shoulders flat on the floor to maximize the stretch in your spine and obliques
2. Move slowly and with control to avoid straining your back
3. Breathe deeply and steadily, exhaling as you lower your knees to the side and inhaling as you bring them back to the center

title: Cable Standing Crunch
summary: Attach a rope to a high pulley, face away from the stack and hold an end in each hand beside your ears.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley, face away from the stack and hold an end in each hand beside your ears.
Stand a step forward with the feet hip width apart and the knees soft, so the cable is under tension. This is the starting position.
Crunch the ribs down toward your hips as you breathe out, rounding the upper back and keeping the hips still.
Let the cable draw you back upright slowly as you breathe in, keeping constant tension on the abdominals.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, using a weight light enough that the lower back does not take over.

title: Cable Standing Lift
summary: Connect a standard handle on a tower, and move the cable to the lowest pulley position.
steps: Connect a standard handle on a tower, and move the cable to the lowest pulley position.

With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Your outstretched arm should be aligned with the cable.
With your feet positioned shoulder width apart, squat down and grab the handle with both hands. Your arms should still be fully extended.
In one motion, pull the handle up and across your body until your arms are in a fully-extended position above your head.
Keep your back straight and your arms close to your body as you pivot your back foot and straighten your legs to get a full range of motion.
Retract your arms and then your body. Return to the neutral position in a slow and controlled manner.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.

title: Crunch on a Bench
summary: Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent and your heels resting on the end of it, hands lightly behind your head.
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent and your heels resting on the end of it, hands lightly behind your head.
Press the lower back into the bench and keep the chin off the chest. This is the starting position.
Curl the head, shoulders and upper back up off the bench as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Lower back down slowly as you breathe in, stopping just before the shoulders touch, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Side Bend
summary: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist. Your feet should be placed at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist. Your feet should be placed at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary.
Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then change hands.
tips: 1. Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement
2. Exhale as you bend to the side and inhale as you return to the starting position
3. Keep your head and neck in a neutral position, facing forward

title: Hanging Straight Leg Hip Raise
summary: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width, arms straight and legs together.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width, arms straight and legs together.
Pull the shoulders down away from your ears and brace the core so the body stops swinging. This is the starting position.
Raise both straight legs until they are level with your hips, then keep going by curling the pelvis up toward your ribs so the hips leave the vertical line.
Lower the hips first and then the legs, slowly and under control, as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the pelvic curl at the top is what separates this from a plain leg raise.

title: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
summary: Hang from a chin-up bar with both arms extended at arms length in top of you using either a wide grip or a medium grip. The legs should be straight down with the pelvis rolled slightly backwards. This will be your starting position.
steps: Hang from a chin-up bar with both arms extended at arms length in top of you using either a wide grip or a medium grip. The legs should be straight down with the pelvis rolled slightly backwards. This will be your starting position.
Raise your legs until the torso makes a 90-degree angle with the legs. Exhale as you perform this movement and hold the contraction for a second or so.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Incline Leg Hip Raise
summary: Set a bench to a slight decline and lie back on it, gripping the top edge or the rollers behind your head.
steps: Set a bench to a slight decline and lie back on it, gripping the top edge or the rollers behind your head.
Raise both legs until they point at the ceiling and press the lower back into the bench. This is the starting position.
Lift the hips off the bench by pushing the feet straight up as you breathe out, using the abdominals rather than swinging the legs.
Lower the hips back to the bench slowly as you breathe in, keeping the legs vertical.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then lower the legs under control.

title: Landmine 180
summary: Position a bar into a landmine or securely anchor it in a corner. Load the bar to an appropriate weight.
steps: Position a bar into a landmine or securely anchor it in a corner. Load the bar to an appropriate weight.
Raise the bar from the floor, taking it to shoulder height with both hands with your arms extended in front of you. Adopt a wide stance. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by rotating the trunk and hips as you swing the weight all the way down to one side. Keep your arms extended throughout the exercise.
Reverse the motion to swing the weight all the way to the opposite side.
Continue alternating the movement until the set is complete.

title: Machine Seated Crunch
summary: Set the seat so the chest pad sits against your upper chest and hook your feet under the rollers.
steps: Set the seat so the chest pad sits against your upper chest and hook your feet under the rollers.
Take the handles above your shoulders and sit tall with the weight already lifted off the stack. This is the starting position.
Curl your ribs down toward your hips as you breathe out, rounding the upper back rather than pulling with the arms.
Return slowly to the upright position as you breathe in, keeping tension on the abdominals, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Seated Leg Raise Crunch
summary: Select a light weight and sit in the crunch machine with your feet under the rollers and your hands on the upper handles.
steps: Select a light weight and sit in the crunch machine with your feet under the rollers and your hands on the upper handles.
Sit tall with the elbows bent and the triceps on the pads. This is the starting position.
Crunch the torso down and lift the legs at the same time as you breathe out, so the ribs and the knees travel toward each other.
Return slowly to the upright position as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Lying Floor Leg Raise
summary: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the hands under your glutes, palms down.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the hands under your glutes, palms down.
Press the lower back into the floor and lift both heels a few centimetres. This is the starting position.
Raise both legs until they are vertical as you breathe out, keeping the knees straight and the lower back down.
Lower the legs slowly as you breathe in, stopping before the heels touch or before the lower back lifts, whichever comes first.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Lying Straight Leg Raise
summary: Lie flat on your back with the arms alongside your body and both legs straight.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the arms alongside your body and both legs straight.
Brace the abdominals so the lower back stays in contact with the floor. This is the starting position.
Raise both straight legs together until they are perpendicular to the floor as you breathe out.
Lower them slowly back down as you breathe in, keeping the knees locked and stopping the moment the lower back tries to arch.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Otis-Up
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet anchored, holding a weight plate against your chest with both hands.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet anchored, holding a weight plate against your chest with both hands.
Press the lower back into the floor. This is the starting position.
Sit all the way up as you breathe out, and as you reach the top press the plate straight overhead.
Bring the plate back to your chest, then lower the torso to the floor slowly as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the plate close to the body so the lower back is not pulled forward.

title: Side Plank
summary: Lie on one side with the forearm on the floor, the elbow directly under the shoulder and the legs stacked.
steps: Lie on one side with the forearm on the floor, the elbow directly under the shoulder and the legs stacked.
Press the forearm and the side of the bottom foot into the floor and lift the hips until the body is a straight line from the ankles to the head. This is the starting position.
Hold the position with the hips high and the top shoulder stacked over the bottom one, breathing steadily.
Hold for 20 to 45 seconds or until the hips start to drop, then lower and repeat on the other side.
tips: 1. Ensure your elbow is directly under your shoulder to support your upper body
2. Focus on keeping your head in line with your spine to prevent neck strain
3. Maintain a straight body line, avoiding any sagging or lifting of the hips
4. Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort

title: Sit-Up on an Exercise Ball
summary: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until the ball supports your lower back, knees bent to a right angle.
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until the ball supports your lower back, knees bent to a right angle.
Cross the arms over your chest or place the hands lightly behind your head. This is the starting position.
Curl the torso up off the ball as you breathe out, lifting the ribs toward the hips rather than pulling on your neck.
Lower back over the ball slowly as you breathe in, letting the abdominals stretch a little at the bottom.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the feet planted so the ball stays still.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and proper form
2. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands to prevent strain; use your core muscles to lift your body
3. Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury

title: Sit-Up
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the arms crossed over your chest.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the arms crossed over your chest.
Press the lower back down and keep the chin a fist's width from your chest. This is the starting position.
Curl the torso all the way up until your chest is close to your thighs as you breathe out, leading with the ribs rather than the head.
Lower back to the floor slowly as you breathe in, one vertebra at a time.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, anchoring the feet only if you cannot keep them down.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maximize muscle engagement and support your lower back
2. Move your body slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to prevent injury
3. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your torso and inhaling as you lower it back down

title: Spell Caster
summary: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip. Your feet should be wide with your hips and knees extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip. Your feet should be wide with your hips and knees extended. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by pulling both of the dumbbells to one side next to your hip, rotating your torso.
Keeping your arms straight and the dumbbells parallel to the ground, rotate your torso to swing the weights to your opposite side.
Continue alternating, rotating from one side to the other until the set is complete.

title: Chin-to-Chest Stretch
summary: Get into a seated position on the floor.
steps: Get into a seated position on the floor.
Place both hands at the rear of your head, fingers interlocked, thumbs pointing down and elbows pointing straight ahead. Slowly pull your head down to your chest. Hold for 20-30 seconds.

title: Iron Cross Stretch
summary: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and both legs straight.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and both legs straight.
Press the shoulder blades into the floor. This is the starting position.
Raise one leg and take it across your body toward the opposite hand, keeping both shoulders down and the knee as straight as is comfortable.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds where the lower back and the outside of the hip stretch, then return and repeat on the other side.
tips: 1. Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort
2. Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury
3. If you have limited flexibility, bend your knee slightly to reduce strain and gradually work towards straightening your leg

title: Seated Twist Stretch - Straight Arm
summary: Sit tall on the floor with both legs straight in front of you and the spine lengthened.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with both legs straight in front of you and the spine lengthened.
Reach both arms straight forward at shoulder height, palms facing down. This is the starting position.
Rotate the torso to one side, keeping the arms straight and level and the hips facing forward, until the waist stretches.
Return to the middle and repeat to the other side, alternating for 8 to 10 turns each way.

title: Spinal Stretch on an Exercise Ball
summary: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward, lying back until the ball supports your mid-back.
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward, lying back until the ball supports your mid-back.
Keep the feet flat on the floor about hip width apart and the knees over the ankles. This is the starting position.
Let the head, arms and shoulders drape back over the ball so the spine extends and the front of the body opens.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then walk the feet back in and curl up to sitting.

title: Standing Side Bend - Bent Arm
summary: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and the knees soft.
steps: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and the knees soft.
Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so the hand rests behind your head. This is the starting position.
Bend sideways away from the raised arm, keeping both hips level and the torso in one plane, until that side of the ribs stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then come back upright and repeat on the other side.

title: Twisting Crunch
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands lightly behind your head.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands lightly behind your head.
Press the lower back into the floor and lift the head and shoulders slightly. This is the starting position.
Curl up and rotate so one shoulder travels toward the opposite knee as you breathe out, turning from the ribs.
Lower back to the floor slowly as you breathe in, then repeat to the other side.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: V-Up
summary: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the arms extended overhead on the floor.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the arms extended overhead on the floor.
Brace the abdominals so the lower back stays down. This is the starting position.
Lift the straight legs and the torso at the same time as you breathe out, reaching the hands toward the feet so the body forms a V.
Lower the arms and legs back to the floor together and under control as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, bending the knees slightly if the lower back arches.
tips: 1. Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift into the 'V' position and inhale as you lower back down
2. Avoid using momentum to lift your legs and torso; focus on using your abdominal muscles
3. Keep your legs and arms straight throughout the movement for maximum effectiveness

title: Vertical Leg Raise on Parallel Bars
summary: Step into the captain's chair and rest your forearms on the pads, gripping the handles with your back against the back pad.
steps: Step into the captain's chair and rest your forearms on the pads, gripping the handles with your back against the back pad.
Let the legs hang straight down and press the shoulders down away from your ears. This is the starting position.
Raise both knees or straight legs toward your chest as you breathe out, curling the pelvis up at the top rather than only bending the hips.
Lower the legs slowly as you breathe in, keeping the back against the pad and stopping any swing before the next repetition.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Weighted Leg Extension Crunch
summary: Lie on your back holding a weight plate or a dumbbell against your chest with both hands, knees bent and feet off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back holding a weight plate or a dumbbell against your chest with both hands, knees bent and feet off the floor.
Press the lower back into the floor and curl the head and shoulders up slightly. This is the starting position.
Extend both legs out straight while lowering the torso a little, keeping the lower back down and the weight on your chest.
Draw the knees back in and crunch the ribs toward them as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the feet off the floor throughout.

title: 45-Degree Hyperextension
summary: Set the pad of a 45-degree back extension bench just below your hip bones and lock your ankles under the rollers.
steps: Set the pad of a 45-degree back extension bench just below your hip bones and lock your ankles under the rollers.
Cross the arms over your chest and hinge forward until your torso hangs down with the back flat. This is the starting position.
Raise the torso by squeezing the glutes and the lower back until the body is in a straight line with the legs, breathing out.
Stop at that line rather than arching past it, then lower slowly back down as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Band Bent-Over Row
summary: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip width apart and take an end in each hand.
steps: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the feet hip width apart and take an end in each hand.
Bend the knees slightly and hinge forward from the hips until the torso is close to parallel with the floor, back flat and head in line with the spine. This is the starting position.
Pull both hands to your waist as you breathe out, keeping the elbows close to the body and squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top.
Straighten the arms slowly back toward the floor as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping
2. Exhale as you pull the band towards your torso and inhale as you lower it back down
3. Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement

title: Band Kneeling One-Arm Pulldown
summary: Anchor a resistance band above head height and kneel far enough back from it that the band is under tension with the arm straight overhead.
steps: Anchor a resistance band above head height and kneel far enough back from it that the band is under tension with the arm straight overhead.
Hold the free end in one hand, brace the core and keep the torso upright. This is the starting position.
Pull the elbow down and toward your ribs as you breathe out, driving with the lat rather than the hand.
Let the arm straighten back overhead slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing sides.

title: Band One-Arm Twisting Seated Row
summary: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and loop a resistance band around the soles of your feet, holding one end in one hand with the palm facing down.
steps: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and loop a resistance band around the soles of your feet, holding one end in one hand with the palm facing down.
Sit tall with the arm straight and the band under tension. This is the starting position.
Pull the elbow back along your ribs as you breathe out, rotating the wrist so the palm faces your torso by the time the hand reaches your waist.
Straighten the arm slowly and rotate the palm back down as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing arms.

title: Band One-Leg Kickback
summary: Kneel on all fours with a resistance band looped around one foot and the other end held under both hands.
steps: Kneel on all fours with a resistance band looped around one foot and the other end held under both hands.
Keep the back flat and the working knee bent to a right angle under your hip. This is the starting position.
Push the working foot back and up against the band until the leg is straight in line with your torso, breathing out and squeezing the glute.
Return the knee slowly under your hip as you breathe in without letting the lower back arch, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.

title: Band Pull Through
summary: Anchor a resistance band low behind you, straddle it with the feet set wide and hold the free end in both hands between your legs.
steps: Anchor a resistance band low behind you, straddle it with the feet set wide and hold the free end in both hands between your legs.
Step forward until the band is under tension and stand with the knees slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Hinge at the hips and reach the hands back between your legs as far as they will go, keeping the back flat and the arms straight.
Stand back up by driving the hips forward and squeezing the glutes, breathing out — all of the movement comes from the hips, not the shoulders.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Band Seated Row
summary: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and a slight bend in the knees, looping a resistance band around the soles of both feet.
steps: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and a slight bend in the knees, looping a resistance band around the soles of both feet.
Hold an end in each hand with the arms straight and sit tall so the band is under tension. This is the starting position.
Pull both hands to your waist as you breathe out, drawing the elbows straight back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Straighten the arms slowly as you breathe in, letting the shoulder blades open without rounding the lower back, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Band Straight-Back Seated Row
summary: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet, holding an end in each hand.
steps: Sit on the floor with the legs extended and loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet, holding an end in each hand.
Sit tall with the spine vertical and the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Pull both hands to your waist as you breathe out while keeping the torso completely upright — unlike the ordinary seated row, the body does not lean back at all.
Straighten the arms slowly as you breathe in without letting the torso follow them forward, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Bent-Over Row - Overhand Grip
summary: Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
steps: Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.

Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Straight-Leg Deadlift
summary: Stand with the feet hip width apart holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
steps: Stand with the feet hip width apart holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Set the back flat, the chest up and the knees almost straight with just a soft bend. This is the starting position.
Push the hips back and lower the bar down the front of your legs as you breathe in, keeping it in contact with them and the back flat.
Stop when the hamstrings will not lengthen further without the lower back rounding, then drive the hips forward to stand up as you breathe out.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, treating any rounding of the back as the end of the set.
tips: 1. Keep your back straight throughout the movement to avoid rounding your spine
2. Focus on hinging at your hips rather than bending your lower back
3. Ensure your knees are slightly bent to avoid locking them and putting stress on your joints

title: Barbell Bent-Over Row - Underhand Grip
summary: Hold a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, palms facing forward, and stand with the feet hip width apart.
steps: Hold a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, palms facing forward, and stand with the feet hip width apart.
Bend the knees slightly and hinge forward from the hips until the torso is at about 45 degrees, back flat and the bar hanging at arm's length. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar into your lower ribs as you breathe out, keeping the elbows tucked close to the body — the underhand grip brings the lower lats into the pull.
Lower the bar slowly back to arm's length as you breathe in without letting the torso rise.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Lat Pulldown - Reverse Grip
summary: Sit at a pulldown station with the thigh pads set snug and take the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
steps: Sit at a pulldown station with the thigh pads set snug and take the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
Sit tall, lean the torso back about 20 degrees and lift the chest. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar to the top of your chest as you breathe out, driving the elbows down and back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Let the bar rise slowly until the arms are straight and the lats are stretched as you breathe in, without letting the shoulders shrug up.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Lat Pulldown - Wide Grip
summary: Sit at a pulldown station with the thigh pads snug and take the wide bar with an overhand grip well outside shoulder width.
steps: Sit at a pulldown station with the thigh pads snug and take the wide bar with an overhand grip well outside shoulder width.
Sit tall with a slight backward lean and the chest lifted. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar down to the top of your chest as you breathe out, leading with the elbows and squeezing the lats at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly to full arm extension as you breathe in, keeping the torso still.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, never pulling the bar behind your neck.

title: Cable One-Arm Lat Pulldown
summary: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and sit or kneel below it, taking the handle in one hand with the palm facing in.
steps: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and sit or kneel below it, taking the handle in one hand with the palm facing in.
Let the arm extend fully overhead so the shoulder blade rises, and brace the core. This is the starting position.
Pull the elbow down toward your ribs as you breathe out, drawing the shoulder blade down first and squeezing the lat.
Let the arm straighten back overhead slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing arms.
tips: 1. Exhale as you pull the handle down and inhale as you extend it back
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine as you pull down
3. Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain

title: Cable One-Arm Twisting Seated Row
summary: To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
steps: To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the single handle attachment with your left arm using a palms-down grip.

With your arm extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lat as you hold the bar in front of you. The right arm can be kept by the waist. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it as you rotate the wrist, so that by the time your hand is by your abdominals it is in a neutral position (palms facing the torso). Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard.

Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in. Tip: Remember to rotate the wrist as you go back to the starting position so that the palms are facing down again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform the same movement with the right hand.

title: Cable Pulldown - Close Underhand Grip
summary: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
steps: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
Grab the pull-down bar with the palms facing your torso (a supinated grip). Make sure that the hands are placed closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

As you breathe out, pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the fully contracted position and keep the elbows close to your body. The upper torso should remain stationary as your bring the bar to you and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, while breathing in, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Seated High Row - V-Bar
summary: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
steps: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Seated Row - Normal Grip
summary: Sit at a low pulley row station with a straight bar attached, feet on the platform and the knees slightly bent.
steps: Sit at a low pulley row station with a straight bar attached, feet on the platform and the knees slightly bent.
