Take the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width and sit up until the arms are straight and the lats are stretched. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar into your abdomen as you breathe out, drawing the elbows straight back past your ribs and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Let the bar travel forward slowly as you breathe in until the arms are straight again, keeping the torso upright rather than following it.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Seated Row - Parallel Grip
summary: Sit at a low pulley row station with a close parallel handle attached and place your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
steps: Sit at a low pulley row station with a close parallel handle attached and place your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Take the handle so the palms face each other and sit up with the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Pull the handle into your navel as you breathe out, keeping the elbows brushing your sides — the neutral grip keeps the shoulders in their strongest position.
Let the handle travel forward slowly as you breathe in until the shoulder blades open, without rounding the lower back.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Seated Row - Wide Grip
summary: Sit at a low pulley row station with a long straight bar attached, feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
steps: Sit at a low pulley row station with a long straight bar attached, feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Take the bar with an overhand grip well outside shoulder width and sit up with the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar into your upper abdomen with the elbows flared out to the sides as you breathe out, squeezing the mid-back and the rear shoulders.
Let the bar travel forward slowly as you breathe in until the arms are straight again.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the wide grip shifts the work from the lats onto the middle of the back.

title: Cable Straight-Back Seated High Row - Reverse Grip
summary: Sit at a row station with the pulley set above shoulder height and take the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
steps: Sit at a row station with the pulley set above shoulder height and take the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
Sit tall with the spine vertical, the feet braced and the arms straight out in front of you. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar down and into your lower ribs as you breathe out, keeping the torso completely upright and the elbows close to your sides.
Let the bar return slowly along the same line as you breathe in, without leaning forward to follow it.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

tips: 1. Keep your back straight and avoid leaning back or using momentum
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement
3. Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you extend it back up

title: Cable Straight-Back Seated Row - V-Grip
summary: Sit at a low pulley row station with a V-handle attached, feet on the platform and the knees slightly bent.
steps: Sit at a low pulley row station with a V-handle attached, feet on the platform and the knees slightly bent.
Take the handle with the palms facing each other and sit up so the spine is vertical and the arms are straight. This is the starting position.
Pull the handle into your navel as you breathe out while keeping the torso perfectly upright — the back never rocks backward to help.
Let the handle travel forward slowly as you breathe in, allowing only the shoulder blades to open.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Chin-Up - Narrow Parallel Grip
summary: Hang from parallel handles or a narrow neutral-grip bar with the palms facing each other and the arms straight.
steps: Hang from parallel handles or a narrow neutral-grip bar with the palms facing each other and the arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down away from your ears and brace the core. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up until your chest is close to the handles, breathing out and keeping the elbows travelling straight down rather than flaring.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the neutral grip is usually the kindest on the elbows and shoulders.

title: Close-Grip Chin-Up
summary: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip and the hands almost touching, arms straight.
steps: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip and the hands almost touching, arms straight.
Pull the shoulder blades down and brace the core so the legs stay still. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the bar, breathing out and keeping the elbows tight to your ribs.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the close grip puts more of the work on the biceps than a shoulder-width chin-up.

title: Commando Pull-Up
summary: Stand under the bar so it runs front to back over your head, and take it with both hands one in front of the other, palms facing each other.
steps: Stand under the bar so it runs front to back over your head, and take it with both hands one in front of the other, palms facing each other.
Hang with the arms straight and the body to one side of the bar. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up alongside the bar so one shoulder passes it and your head comes up on that side, breathing out.
Lower slowly to a full hang, then repeat pulling up on the other side.
Keep alternating sides for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your head above the bar at the top
2. Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury
3. Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain
4. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself

title: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
summary: With a dumbbell in each hand (palms facing your torso), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward by bending at the waist; as you bend make sure to keep your back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The weights should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
steps: With a dumbbell in each hand (palms facing your torso), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward by bending at the waist; as you bend make sure to keep your back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The weights should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.

While keeping the torso stationary, lift the dumbbells to your side (as you breathe out), keeping the elbows close to the body (do not exert any force with the forearm other than holding the weights). On the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the weight again to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement
2. Breathe out as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and breathe in as you lower them back down
3. Ensure your elbows remain close to your body throughout the exercise to protect your joints

title: Dumbbell Deadlift
summary: Stand with the feet hip width apart and a dumbbell on the floor outside each foot.
steps: Stand with the feet hip width apart and a dumbbell on the floor outside each foot.
Push the hips back, bend the knees and take a dumbbell in each hand with the back flat, the chest up and the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Stand up by driving the floor away with the legs and extending the hips, breathing out and keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.
Reverse the movement to set the dumbbells back down, breathing in and letting the hips travel back before the knees bend.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the back flat on every one.

title: Dumbbell Hammer-Grip Incline Bench Row
summary: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
steps: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Let the arms hang straight down and press the chest into the pad. This is the starting position.
Row both dumbbells up to your ribs as you breathe out, keeping the elbows close to the body and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to arm's length as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the chest support removes the lower back from the movement entirely.

title: Dumbbell Incline Row
summary: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
steps: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.
tips: 1. Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and avoid swinging
2. Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms
3. Select a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise

title: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
summary: Set a bench to a shallow incline and lie face down on it with a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight below your shoulders.
steps: Set a bench to a shallow incline and lie face down on it with a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight below your shoulders.
Turn the palms to face your feet and keep the chest on the pad. This is the starting position.
Row both dumbbells up with the elbows flared out to the sides, so the upper arms finish level with your shoulders, breathing out.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to arm's length as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; flaring the elbows is what moves the work from the lats to the rear shoulders.
tips: 1. Avoid using momentum to lift the weights; use controlled motions for effective muscle engagement
2. Breathe out as you lift the dumbbells and breathe in as you lower them
3. Ensure your body remains stable on the bench and avoid lifting your chest

title: Dumbbell Palm-Rotational Bent-Over Row
summary: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing back, then hinge forward from the hips until the torso is close to parallel with the floor.
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing back, then hinge forward from the hips until the torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length with the back flat and the head in line with the spine. This is the starting position.
Row both dumbbells to your ribs as you breathe out, rotating the wrists as you pull so the palms face your torso at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly and rotate the palms back to face behind you as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Reverse-Grip Row
summary: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing forward, feet hip width apart.
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing forward, feet hip width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips to about 45 degrees with the back flat and the arms hanging straight. This is the starting position.
Pull both dumbbells into your lower ribs as you breathe out, keeping the elbows tucked tight to your sides.
Lower them slowly back to arm's length as you breathe in without letting the torso rise.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
summary: Grasp a couple of dumbbells holding them by your side at arm's length.
steps: Grasp a couple of dumbbells holding them by your side at arm's length.
Stand with your torso straight and your legs spaced using a shoulder width or narrower stance. The knees should be slightly bent. This is your starting position.

Keeping the knees stationary, lower the dumbbells to over the top of your feet by bending at the waist while keeping your back straight. Keep moving forward as if you were going to pick something from the floor until you feel a stretch on the hamstrings. Exhale as you perform this movement
Start bringing your torso up straight again by extending your hips and waist until you are back at the starting position. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders
2. Engage your core throughout the exercise for stability
3. Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist

title: Hammer-Grip Pull-Up
summary: Hang from two parallel handles with the palms facing each other and the arms straight.
steps: Hang from two parallel handles with the palms facing each other and the arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down away from your ears and squeeze the glutes so the body stays rigid. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up until your chin is level with the handles, breathing out and keeping the elbows driving straight down.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Inverted Row Between Chairs
summary: Wedge a solid bar or broom handle between two sturdy chairs at about hip height and check that it takes your weight before you hang from it.
steps: Wedge a solid bar or broom handle between two sturdy chairs at about hip height and check that it takes your weight before you hang from it.
Lie underneath and take the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder width, heels on the floor and the body straight. This is the starting position.
Pull your chest to the bar as you breathe out, squeezing the shoulder blades together and keeping the hips level with the shoulders.
Lower yourself slowly until the arms are straight as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, bending the knees to make it easier.

title: Kettlebell Deadlift
summary: Stand with the feet hip width apart and a kettlebell on the floor between your arches.
steps: Stand with the feet hip width apart and a kettlebell on the floor between your arches.
Push the hips back, bend the knees and take the handle with both hands, arms straight, back flat and chest up. This is the starting position.
Stand up by driving through the whole foot and extending the hips, breathing out and keeping the bell close to your shins.
Push the hips back to lower the bell to the floor as you breathe in, letting the knees bend only after the hips have travelled back.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Back Extension
summary: Set the seat and the roller of the back extension machine so the pad sits across your upper back and your feet reach the platform.
steps: Set the seat and the roller of the back extension machine so the pad sits across your upper back and your feet reach the platform.
Sit tall with the belt fastened if the machine has one, and cross the arms over your chest. This is the starting position.
Push back against the pad by extending the hips and the lower back until the torso is roughly in line with the thighs, breathing out.
Return slowly to the upright position as you breathe in, without letting the weight pull you into a rounded back.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your movements slow and controlled to maintain proper form and maximize muscle engagement
2. Avoid hyperextending your back; stop when your body forms a straight line to prevent strain on your lower back
3. Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to support your spine and maintain stability

title: Machine High Row
summary: Set the chest pad of the high row machine so the handles start just above shoulder height when you sit down.
steps: Set the chest pad of the high row machine so the handles start just above shoulder height when you sit down.
Take a handle in each hand with the arms straight and the chest pressed into the pad. This is the starting position.
Pull the handles down and back toward your ribs as you breathe out, driving with the elbows and squeezing the lats.
Let the handles travel back up and forward slowly as you breathe in until the shoulder blades open.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Reverse-Grip T-Bar Row
summary: Load the T-bar row, stand on the platform and lie your chest against the support pad with the feet flat.
steps: Load the T-bar row, stand on the platform and lie your chest against the support pad with the feet flat.
Take the handles with an underhand grip and let the arms hang straight down. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar up into your abdomen as you breathe out, keeping the elbows tucked close to your sides and the chest on the pad.
Lower the bar slowly back to arm's length as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the underhand grip brings the lower lats into the pull.

title: Machine T-Bar Row
summary: Load up the T-bar Row Machine with the desired weight and adjust the leg height so that your upper chest is at the top of the pad. Tip: In some machines all you can do is stand on the appropriate step that allows you to be at a height that has the upper chest at the top of the pad.
steps: Load up the T-bar Row Machine with the desired weight and adjust the leg height so that your upper chest is at the top of the pad. Tip: In some machines all you can do is stand on the appropriate step that allows you to be at a height that has the upper chest at the top of the pad.
Lay face down on the pad and grab the handles. You can either use a palms down, palms up, or palms in position depending on what part of your back you want to emphasize.
Lift the bar off the rack and extend your arms in front of you. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale slowly pull the weight up and squeeze your back at the top of the movement. Tip: Keep the upper arms as close to the torso as possible throughout the movement in order to better engage the back muscles. Also, do not lift your body off of the pad at any time and refrain from using the biceps to lift the weight.
After a second contraction at the top of the movement, as you inhale, slowly go back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Pull-Up - Wide Grip Behind the Neck
summary: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip set well outside shoulder width, arms straight.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip set well outside shoulder width, arms straight.
Pull the shoulder blades down and keep the torso vertical, chin tucked slightly. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up so the bar passes behind your head and stop when it is level with the base of your neck, breathing out.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, and use the front version instead if the shoulders feel pinched at the top -- behind-the-neck pulling asks for a lot of shoulder rotation.

title: Pull-Up - Wide Grip to the Chest
summary: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip set well outside shoulder width, arms straight and ankles crossed.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip set well outside shoulder width, arms straight and ankles crossed.
Pull the shoulder blades down away from your ears and brace the core. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up by driving the elbows down and back until your upper chest is close to the bar, breathing out and keeping the chest lifted.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in, resisting all the way.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the wide grip puts most of the work on the lats.

title: Reverse-Grip Machine Lat Pulldown
summary: Sit at the lat pulldown station and set the thigh pads so they hold you down firmly.
steps: Sit at the lat pulldown station and set the thigh pads so they hold you down firmly.
Take the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width, sit tall and lean back about 20 degrees. This is the starting position.
Pull the bar to the top of your chest as you breathe out, driving the elbows down and back and squeezing the lats at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly to full arm extension as you breathe in, keeping the torso still.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Reverse-Grip Pull-Up
summary: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width and the arms straight.
steps: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width and the arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down, brace the core and cross the ankles. This is the starting position.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, breathing out and leading with the chest rather than the head.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang as you breathe in, resisting all the way down.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Ring High Row
summary: Set a pair of rings or suspension handles at about chest height and take one in each hand with the palms facing down.
steps: Set a pair of rings or suspension handles at about chest height and take one in each hand with the palms facing down.
Walk the feet forward and lean back with the arms straight, body in a straight line from the heels to the head. This is the starting position.
Pull your chest toward the handles with the elbows flared out to shoulder height, breathing out and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself slowly until the arms are straight again as you breathe in, keeping the hips from sagging.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; walk the feet back to make it easier.

title: Single-Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
summary: Stand with the feet hip width apart holding one dumbbell in both hands in front of your thighs.
steps: Stand with the feet hip width apart holding one dumbbell in both hands in front of your thighs.
Set the back flat, the chest up and the knees almost straight. This is the starting position.
Push the hips back and lower the dumbbell down the front of your legs as you breathe in, keeping it close to them.
Stop when the hamstrings will not lengthen further without the back rounding, then drive the hips forward to stand up as you breathe out.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Smith Machine Deadlift
summary: Set the bar of the Smith machine at the lowest position and stand with the feet hip width apart, shins close to it.
steps: Set the bar of the Smith machine at the lowest position and stand with the feet hip width apart, shins close to it.
Push the hips back, bend the knees and take the bar with an overhand grip just outside your legs, back flat and chest up. This is the starting position.
Stand up by pushing the floor away with the legs and extending the hips, breathing out and unlocking the bar as it leaves the catches.
Lower the bar along the rails by pushing the hips back first and then bending the knees, breathing in and keeping the back flat.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then rotate the bar back into its hooks at the bottom.

title: Dynamic Back Stretch
summary: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, swing them straight up in front of you 5-10 times, increasing the range of motion each time until your arms are above your head.
tips: 1. Keep your back straight throughout the movement to ensure a proper stretch and prevent strain
2. Focus on pushing your hips downwards rather than bending at the waist to enhance the stretch in your back
3. Use controlled movements to avoid jerking or sudden motions that could lead to injury

title: Elbows Back Stretch
summary: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and interlace the fingers behind your head.
steps: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and interlace the fingers behind your head.
Lift the chest and keep the chin level. This is the starting position.
Draw both elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades together until the upper back and the front of the chest lengthen.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: 1. Engage your core muscles to support your lower back as you lean backward
2. Avoid overextending your lower back; only lean back as far as comfortable without causing pain
3. Breathe deeply throughout the exercise, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean back

title: Kneeling Lat Stretch
summary: Kneel in front of a bench or a low box, about an arm's length away, and place both hands on its edge.
steps: Kneel in front of a bench or a low box, about an arm's length away, and place both hands on its edge.
Sit the hips back toward your heels and keep the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Let the chest sink toward the floor between your arms until you feel the stretch along the sides of your back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then sit up to release.

title: Middle Back Stretch
summary: Stand so your feet are shoulder width apart and your hands are on your hips.
steps: Stand so your feet are shoulder width apart and your hands are on your hips.
Twist at your waist until you feel a stretch. Hold for 10 to 15 seconds, then twist to the other side.

title: Seated Lower Back Stretch
summary: Sit on the front edge of a bench or chair with the feet flat and set wider than your hips.
steps: Sit on the front edge of a bench or chair with the feet flat and set wider than your hips.
Sit tall and rest your hands on your thighs. This is the starting position.
Bend forward between your knees and let the arms and head hang toward the floor so the lower back rounds gently.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then roll up one vertebra at a time.

title: Seated Wide Angle Pose Sequence
summary: Sit on the floor and open both legs as wide as is comfortable, knees and toes pointing up.
steps: Sit on the floor and open both legs as wide as is comfortable, knees and toes pointing up.
Sit tall on your sitting bones with the hands on the floor in front of you. This is the starting position.
Walk the hands forward between your legs and fold from the hips, holding for 20 to 30 seconds.
Walk the hands over toward one foot and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then repeat toward the other foot.
Come back to the middle, close the legs and shake them out.

title: Sitting Bent-Over Back Stretch
summary: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you and the feet hip width apart.
steps: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you and the feet hip width apart.
Sit tall and lengthen the spine upward. This is the starting position.
Fold forward from the hips and reach the hands toward your feet, letting the back round softly and the head hang.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then roll up slowly to sitting.

title: Spine Stretch
summary: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
steps: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Set the spine level from the tailbone to the head. This is the starting position.
Round the back up toward the ceiling as you breathe out, dropping the head and tucking the tailbone under.
Reverse it as you breathe in, letting the belly drop and the chest and tailbone lift so the spine arches the other way.
Alternate slowly for 8 to 10 breaths.

title: Spine Stretch Forward
summary: Sit tall on the floor with the legs extended a little wider than your hips and the feet flexed.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with the legs extended a little wider than your hips and the feet flexed.
Reach both arms straight forward at shoulder height. This is the starting position.
Drop the chin and roll the spine forward one vertebra at a time as you breathe out, reaching the hands along the floor between your legs.
Roll back up to sitting tall the same way as you breathe in, stacking the spine from the base upward.
Repeat for 5 to 8 slow repetitions.

title: Standing Back Rotation Stretch
summary: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and the knees soft, arms bent and held in front of your chest.
steps: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and the knees soft, arms bent and held in front of your chest.
Brace the core and keep the hips facing forward. This is the starting position.
Rotate the upper body to one side as far as it will comfortably go, letting the head follow the chest.
Return to the middle and rotate to the other side, alternating for 20 to 30 seconds.

title: Standing Lateral Stretch
summary: Take a slightly wider than hip distance stance with your knees slightly bent.
steps: Take a slightly wider than hip distance stance with your knees slightly bent.
Place your right hand on your right hip to support the spine.
Raise your left arm in a vertical line and place your left hand behind your head. Keep it there as you incline your torso to the right.
Keep your weight evenly distributed between both legs (don't lean into your left hip). Switch sides.
tips: 1. Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk
2. Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves
3. Focus on keeping your back straight and avoiding excessive rounding of your spine

title: Barbell Drag Curl
summary: Stand upright holding a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, the bar resting against your thighs.
steps: Stand upright holding a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, the bar resting against your thighs.
Set the chest up and the elbows at your sides. This is the starting position.
Curl the bar up while dragging it along your body, letting the elbows travel back behind you so the bar stays in contact with the torso.
Stop when the bar reaches the lower chest, hold for a second, then lower it back down the same path as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the drag keeps the front shoulders out of the lift, so use less weight than a standard curl.
tips: 1. Keep your elbows back to ensure the barbell stays close to your torso throughout the movement
2. Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum
3. Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture

title: Barbell Prone Incline Curl
summary: Set an incline bench and lie face down on it with your chest against the pad and your shoulders near the top edge.
steps: Set an incline bench and lie face down on it with your chest against the pad and your shoulders near the top edge.
Take a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width and let your arms hang straight down, perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.
Keeping the upper arms still, curl the bar up toward your shoulders as you breathe out, and squeeze the biceps for a second at the top.
Lower the bar slowly until the arms are fully extended again as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable One-Arm Curl
summary: Start out by grabbing single handle next to the low pulley machine. Make sure you are far enough from the machine so that your arm is supporting the weight.
steps: Start out by grabbing single handle next to the low pulley machine. Make sure you are far enough from the machine so that your arm is supporting the weight.

Make sure that your upper arm is stationary, perpendicular to the floor with elbows in and palms facing forward. Your non lifting arm should be grabbing your waist. This will allow you to keep your balance.
Slowly begin to curl the single handle upwards while keeping the upper arm stationary until your forearm touches your bicep while exhaling. Tip: Only the forearm should move.
Hold the contraction position as you squeeze the bicep and then lower the single handle back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms while performing this exercise.
tips: 1. Keep your elbow close to your torso throughout the exercise
2. Exhale as you curl the handle up and inhale as you lower it back down
3. Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement

title: Standing Cable Inner Biceps Curl
summary: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand upright holding it with an underhand grip, hands set wider than your shoulders.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand upright holding it with an underhand grip, hands set wider than your shoulders.
Keep the elbows tucked against your sides and the wrists straight, with the bar resting against your thighs. This is the starting position.
Curl the bar up to shoulder height as you breathe out, moving only the forearms, and squeeze for a second — the wide grip biases the inner head of the biceps.
Lower the bar slowly back to full extension as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Seated Alternating Curl
summary: Sit on the end of a bench with the feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell hanging at arm's length in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
steps: Sit on the end of a bench with the feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell hanging at arm's length in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Sit tall with the elbows close to your sides. This is the starting position.
Curl one dumbbell up, rotating the palm to face your shoulder as it rises, and squeeze the biceps for a second at the top as you breathe out.
Lower it slowly back to your thigh as you breathe in, rotating the palm back in, then repeat with the other arm.
Keep alternating until you have completed the prescribed amount of repetitions with each arm; sitting stops the hips from helping the weight up.

title: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
summary: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
summary: Sit down on a flat bench with one dumbbell in front of you between your legs. Your legs should be spread with your knees bent and feet on the floor.
steps: Sit down on a flat bench with one dumbbell in front of you between your legs. Your legs should be spread with your knees bent and feet on the floor.

Use your right arm to pick the dumbbell up. Place the back of your right upper arm on the top of your inner right thigh. Rotate the palm of your hand until it is facing forward away from your thigh. Tip: Your arm should be extended and the dumbbell should be above the floor. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Tip: At the top of the movement make sure that the little finger of your arm is higher than your thumb. This guarantees a good contraction. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in. Caution: Avoid swinging motions at any time.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions. Then repeat the movement with the left arm.
tips: 1. Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the movement to maximize muscle activation
2. Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning back as you lift the weight
3. Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form and without straining

title: Dumbbell Cross-Body Hammer Curl
summary: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand. Your hands should be down at your side with your palms facing in.
steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand. Your hands should be down at your side with your palms facing in.

While keeping your palms facing in and without twisting your arm, curl the dumbbell of the right arm up towards your left shoulder as you exhale. Touch the top of the dumbbell to your shoulder and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path as you inhale and then repeat the same movement for the left arm.
Continue alternating in this fashion until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed for each arm.

title: Dumbbell Incline Biceps Curl
summary: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind the line of your body.
steps: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind the line of your body.
Turn the palms to face forward and let the shoulders settle back into the pad. This is the starting position.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders as you breathe out, keeping the upper arms hanging still so only the forearms move.
Lower them slowly all the way back to a full stretch as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the incline holds the arms behind you, which stretches the long head of the biceps.

title: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
summary: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
steps: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
Turn the palms to face each other and keep them that way for the whole set. This is the starting position.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders as you breathe out without rotating the wrists, so the thumbs stay on top.
Lower them slowly back to a full stretch as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions; the neutral grip shifts work onto the brachialis and the forearms.

title: Dumbbell Preacher Curl Over an Exercise Ball
summary: Kneel behind a stability ball and drape the backs of your upper arms over the top of it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing up.
steps: Kneel behind a stability ball and drape the backs of your upper arms over the top of it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing up.
Let the arms straighten so the dumbbells hang below the ball and your armpits rest against its top. This is the starting position.
Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders as you breathe out, keeping the upper arms pinned to the ball, and squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the elbows are almost straight as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

tips: 1. Keep your upper arms pressed firmly against the exercise ball to isolate the biceps
2. Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement
3. Exhale as you curl the dumbbells upward and inhale as you lower them back down

title: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
summary: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way).
steps: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way).
Let your arms extend and hang naturally in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the floor.
Now keep your elbows in by your side and face the palms forward. This will be your starting position.

Raise the dumbbells by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and ensure that only the forearms move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
tips: 1. Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize bicep engagement
2. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms
3. Avoid swinging the weights to isolate the biceps during the curl

title: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl
summary: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in one hand and lay the back of that upper arm flat on the pad, armpit against the top edge.
steps: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in one hand and lay the back of that upper arm flat on the pad, armpit against the top edge.
Extend the arm until the elbow is almost straight, palm facing up. This is the starting position.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder as you breathe out without letting the upper arm lift off the pad, and squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbell slowly back to the stretched position as you breathe in, repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then change arms.
tips: 1. Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad to isolate the biceps
2. Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms
3. Avoid locking your elbows at the bottom of the movement

title: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
summary: Stand upright holding an EZ curl bar on the angled inner grips with your palms facing up and your elbows tucked against your sides.
steps: Stand upright holding an EZ curl bar on the angled inner grips with your palms facing up and your elbows tucked against your sides.
Let the bar hang at arm's length in front of your thighs, shoulders back and chest up. This is the starting position.
Curl the bar up to shoulder height as you breathe out, keeping the upper arms still so only the forearms move, and squeeze the biceps for a second.
Lower the bar slowly back to full extension as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Lying Supine Dumbbell Curl
summary: Lie down on a flat bench face up while holding a dumbbell in each arm on top of your thighs.
steps: Lie down on a flat bench face up while holding a dumbbell in each arm on top of your thighs.
Bring the dumbbells to the sides with the arms extended and the palms of the hands facing your thighs (neutral grip).

While keeping the arms close to your torso and elbows in, slowly lower your arms (as you keep them extended with a slight bend at the elbows) as far down towards the floor as you can go. Once you cannot go down any further, lock your upper arms in that position and that will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, slowly begin to curl the weights up as you simultaneously rotate your wrists so that the palms of the hands face up. Continue curling the weight until your biceps are fully contracted and squeeze hard at the top position for a second. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Upper arms should remain stationary and elbows should stay in throughout the movement.
Return back to the starting position very slowly.
tips: 1. Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to ensure maximum bicep engagement
2. Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled motion throughout the exercise
3. Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise

title: Butterfly Yoga Pose
summary: Sit tall on the floor, bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together in front of you, drawing the heels toward your groin.
steps: Sit tall on the floor, bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together in front of you, drawing the heels toward your groin.
Hold your feet with both hands and lengthen your spine so you are sitting on top of your sitting bones. This is the starting position.
Let both knees fall toward the floor and breathe steadily, allowing the inner thighs to release rather than pressing the knees down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then bring the knees back together and release.
tips: 1. Maintain a gentle arch in your back while leaning forward to ensure a proper stretch and avoid straining
2. Inhale deeply and exhale slowly throughout the pose to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch
3. Apply gentle pressure to your knees without forcing them down to prevent overstraining your hip joints

title: Barbell Clean and Press
summary: Assume a shoulder-width stance, with knees inside the arms. Now while keeping the back flat, bend at the knees and hips so that you can grab the bar with the arms fully extended and a pronated grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width. Point the elbows out to sides. The bar should be close to the shins. Position the shoulders over or slightly ahead of the bar. Establish a flat back posture. This will be your starting position.
steps: Assume a shoulder-width stance, with knees inside the arms. Now while keeping the back flat, bend at the knees and hips so that you can grab the bar with the arms fully extended and a pronated grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width. Point the elbows out to sides. The bar should be close to the shins. Position the shoulders over or slightly ahead of the bar. Establish a flat back posture. This will be your starting position.

Begin to pull the bar by extending the knees. Move your hips forward and raise the shoulders at the same rate while keeping the angle of the back constant; continue to lift the bar straight up while keeping it close to your body.

As the bar passes the knee, extend at the ankles, knees, and hips forcefully, similar to a jumping motion. As you do so, continue to guide the bar with your hands, shrugging your shoulders and using the momentum from your movement to pull the bar as high as possible. The bar should travel close to your body, and you should keep your elbows out.

At maximum elevation, your feet should clear the floor and you should start to pull yourself under the bar. The mechanics of this could change slightly, depending on the weight used. You should descend into a squatting position as you pull yourself under the bar.

As the bar hits terminal height, rotate your elbows around and under the bar. Rack the bar across the front of the shoulders while keeping the torso erect and flexing the hips and knees to absorb the weight of the bar.
Stand to full height, holding the bar in the clean position.
Without moving your feet, press the bar overhead as you exhale. Lower the bar under control .
tips: 1. Focus on leg drive during the clean to generate power from your lower body
2. Keep your grip firm but not too tight to allow smooth wrist rotation during the clean
3. Exhale powerfully as you press the bar overhead to stabilize your core

title: Donkey Calf Raise
summary: For this exercise you will need access to a donkey calf raise machine. Start by positioning your lower back and hips under the padded lever provided. The tailbone area should be the one making contact with the pad.
steps: For this exercise you will need access to a donkey calf raise machine. Start by positioning your lower back and hips under the padded lever provided. The tailbone area should be the one making contact with the pad.

Place both of your arms on the side handles and place the balls of your feet on the calf block with the heels extending off. Align the toes forward, inward or outward, depending on the area you wish to target, and straighten the knees without locking them. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Ensure your grip on the bench is secure to maintain balance and focus the effort on your calves
2. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders to prevent unnecessary strain on your back
3. Emphasize the upward and downward movements equally to enhance muscle growth and strength in your calves
4. Maintain a slow, controlled pace to increase the intensity of the muscle contraction and effectiveness of the exercise

title: Dumbbell Front Squat
summary: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).
steps: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Ensure your elbows stay up and forward to keep the dumbbells stable on your shoulders
2. Avoid letting your knees collapse inward; keep them aligned with your toes
3. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back

title: Dumbbell Single-Leg Calf Raise
summary: Hang on to a sturdy object for balance and stand on a dumbbell handle, preferably one with round plates so that it rolls as in this manner you have to work harder to stabilize yourself; thus increasing the effectiveness of the exercise.
steps: Hang on to a sturdy object for balance and stand on a dumbbell handle, preferably one with round plates so that it rolls as in this manner you have to work harder to stabilize yourself; thus increasing the effectiveness of the exercise.
Now roll your foot slightly forward so that you can get a nice stretch of the calf. This will be your starting position.

Lift the calf as you roll your foot over the top of the handle so that you get a full extension. Exhale during the execution of this movement. Contract the calf hard at the top and hold for a second. Tip: As you come up, roll the dumbbell slightly backward.
Now inhale as you roll the dumbbell slightly forward as you come down to get a better stretch.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise
summary: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. Place the ball of the foot on a sturdy and stable wooden board (that is around 2-3 inches tall) while your heels extend off and touch the floor. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. Place the ball of the foot on a sturdy and stable wooden board (that is around 2-3 inches tall) while your heels extend off and touch the floor. This will be your starting position.

With the toes pointing either straight (to hit all parts equally), inwards (for emphasis on the outer head) or outwards (for emphasis on the inner head), raise the heels off the floor as you exhale by contracting the calves. Hold the top contraction for a second.
As you inhale, go back to the starting position by slowly lowering the heels.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
tips: 1. Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement
2. Avoid bouncing at the top or bottom of the movement
3. Maintain a straight posture throughout the exercise

title: Sled 45-Degree Calf Press
summary: Sit in the 45-degree leg press and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform, hip width apart, with the heels hanging off.
steps: Sit in the 45-degree leg press and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform, hip width apart, with the heels hanging off.
Press the platform up, release the safety catches and straighten the legs without locking the knees. This is the starting position.
Push the platform away by extending the ankles as far as they will go as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Let the platform come back slowly as you breathe in, until the heels drop below the toes and the calves are fully stretched.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the knees still throughout.

title: Calf Stretch with a Rope
summary: Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front of you and loop a rope around the ball of that foot, holding an end in each hand.
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front of you and loop a rope around the ball of that foot, holding an end in each hand.
Sit tall with the knee straight and the heel resting on the floor. This is the starting position.
Pull gently on the rope so the toes draw back toward your shin, until you feel the stretch through the calf.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release and change legs.
tips: 1. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles
2. Use a moderate amount of tension on the rope to ensure a good stretch without causing discomfort or pain
3. Focus on feeling the stretch in your calf muscle, not your lower back or hamstrings

title: Lying Calf Stretch with a Strap
summary: Lie on your back with one leg bent and that foot flat on the floor, and loop a strap around the ball of the other foot.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg bent and that foot flat on the floor, and loop a strap around the ball of the other foot.
Raise the strapped leg until it is roughly vertical, keeping the knee straight, and hold an end of the strap in each hand. This is the starting position.
Pull the strap gently so the toes come toward your shin, until the calf and the back of the knee feel a steady stretch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, then lower the leg and change sides.

title: Knee Circles
summary: Stand with your feet together, bend the knees slightly and rest your hands on top of them.
steps: Stand with your feet together, bend the knees slightly and rest your hands on top of them.
Keep both feet flat on the floor and your back straight. This is the starting position.
Draw slow circles with the knees, letting the knees and ankles travel through their full comfortable range.
Complete 10 circles in one direction, then 10 in the other.

title: Feet and Ankle Rotations
summary: Sit on a bench or a mat and lift one foot clear of the floor, straightening the knee as far as is comfortable.
steps: Sit on a bench or a mat and lift one foot clear of the floor, straightening the knee as far as is comfortable.
Hold the leg still so the movement happens at the ankle only. This is the starting position.
Rotate the foot slowly through a full circle, leading with the big toe and using the whole range.
Do 10 circles in each direction, then change legs.

title: Feet and Ankle Stretch
summary: Kneel on a mat with the tops of your feet flat on the floor and sit back onto your heels.
steps: Kneel on a mat with the tops of your feet flat on the floor and sit back onto your heels.
Keep the torso upright and your weight settled evenly on both shins. This is the starting position.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds to stretch the front of the ankles and the tops of the feet.
Come up, tuck the toes under so they point forward, then sit back again for another 20 to 30 seconds to stretch the soles.

title: Peroneals Stretch
summary: In a seated position, loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. This will be your starting position.
steps: In a seated position, loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. This will be your starting position.

With the leg extended and the heel off of the ground, pull on the belt so that the foot is inverted, with the inside of the foot being pulled towards you. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then switch sides.

title: Seated Calf Stretch
summary: Sit up straight on an exercise mat.
steps: Sit up straight on an exercise mat.
Bend one knee and put that foot on the floor to stabilize the torso.
Straighten your other leg and flex your ankle.
Using a band, towel, or your hand if you can reach, pull the toes toward you. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.
tips: 1. Focus on maintaining a straight back to enhance the effectiveness of the stretch
2. Ensure your movements are slow and controlled to prevent overstretching or injury
3. If you find it difficult to reach your toes, use a towel or strap for assistance without forcing the stretch
4. Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary tension

title: Stairs Calf Stretch
summary: Stand on a step with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging over it, holding the rail for balance.
steps: Stand on a step with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging over it, holding the rail for balance.
Straighten the knees and take your weight evenly on both feet. This is the starting position.
Let the heels sink below the level of the step until you feel a steady stretch through both calves.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then rise back up and repeat once with the knees slightly bent to reach the deeper soleus.

title: Standing Bench Calf Stretch
summary: Stand facing a bench and place the ball of one foot on its edge with the heel low and that leg straight.
steps: Stand facing a bench and place the ball of one foot on its edge with the heel low and that leg straight.
Keep the other foot flat on the floor and hold the bench for balance. This is the starting position.
Shift your weight gently forward over the front foot until the calf of that leg stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then change legs.

title: Burpee
summary: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms at your sides.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms at your sides.
Squat down and place both hands on the floor just outside your feet, then jump the feet back into a push-up position with the body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the floor and press back up, keeping the hips level with the shoulders.
Jump the feet back under your hips, then drive through the legs into a jump with the arms overhead.
Land softly with the knees bent and move straight into the next repetition.
tips: 1. Start with a moderate pace to master the form, then gradually increase your speed as you become more comfortable with the movement
2. Ensure your movements are fluid and controlled to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints
3. Focus on landing softly during the jump to reduce impact on your knees and ankles

title: Elliptical Trainer Workout
summary: Step onto the elliptical, set your feet flat in the middle of the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.
steps: Step onto the elliptical, set your feet flat in the middle of the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.
Stand tall with the chest up and the core braced, then start the stride and pick a resistance you can hold for the whole session.
Push and pull through the handles in time with the legs, keeping the heels down and the movement smooth rather than bouncing.
Hold a steady pace for the planned time, or alternate one minute hard with two minutes easy for intervals.
Ease the resistance down for the last two minutes to cool off, and step off only once the pedals have stopped.

title: Jump Rope
summary: Hold a handle in each hand with the rope behind your heels and your elbows close to your sides.
steps: Hold a handle in each hand with the rope behind your heels and your elbows close to your sides.
Stand tall with the feet together and the knees soft. This is the starting position.
Turn the rope with the wrists rather than the arms, and hop just high enough to clear it — a couple of centimetres is enough.
Land on the balls of the feet with the knees slightly bent, and keep the rhythm even.
Skip for the planned time or number of turns, resting whenever the rhythm breaks down.

title: Jump Step-Up
summary: Stand facing a sturdy box or step about one foot's distance away, arms at your sides.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or step about one foot's distance away, arms at your sides.
Place one whole foot on the box with the knee bent and leave the other foot on the floor. This is the starting position.
Drive hard through the top leg and jump straight up off the box, swapping the legs in the air.
Land softly with the other foot on the box and the first foot back on the floor, absorbing the landing with a bent knee.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions, and stop the set once the landings stop being quiet.

title: Jumping Jack
summary: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms hanging at your sides.
steps: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms hanging at your sides.
Brace the core and keep the knees soft. This is the starting position.
Jump the feet out to a little wider than shoulder width while sweeping the arms out and overhead.
Jump the feet back together and bring the arms back down in one continuous movement.
Repeat at a steady rhythm for the prescribed time or amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the exercise to absorb impact and reduce strain on your joints
2. Keep your movements light and quick to enhance cardiovascular benefits
3. Engage your shoulders and back muscles when raising your arms to ensure full range of motion
4. Keep your gaze forward and your head in a neutral position to maintain alignment

title: Running
summary: Start with five minutes of brisk walking or easy jogging to warm the legs up.
steps: Start with five minutes of brisk walking or easy jogging to warm the legs up.
Run with the torso tall and the shoulders relaxed, elbows bent to about 90 degrees, letting the arms swing forward and back rather than across the body.
Land with the foot under your hips rather than out in front, and keep the cadence quick and light.
Hold a pace at which you could still speak in short sentences, for the planned distance or time.
Finish with five minutes of easy walking to bring the heart rate down.
tips: 1. Stay hydrated and take breaks, especially during longer runs
2. Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the run
3. Focus on maintaining a relaxed posture and avoid tensing your shoulders

title: Stationary Bike
summary: Set the saddle height so that your knee stays slightly bent when the pedal is at its lowest point.
steps: Set the saddle height so that your knee stays slightly bent when the pedal is at its lowest point.
Sit with your hands resting on the bars, the back straight and the balls of the feet over the pedal axles. This is the starting position.
Pedal smoothly at a comfortable resistance for five minutes to warm up.
Raise the resistance to your working level and hold a cadence of roughly 80 to 90 revolutions per minute for the planned time.
Drop the resistance for the last five minutes and pedal easily to cool down.
tips: 1. Maintain good posture by keeping your back straight and shoulders relaxed to avoid strain
2. Start with a lower resistance level if you are a beginner and gradually increase it as you build strength and endurance
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling deeply and exhaling fully

title: Bridge Pose
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor hip width apart and the heels close to your glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor hip width apart and the heels close to your glutes.
Rest the arms alongside the body with the palms down and press the shoulders gently into the mat. This is the starting position.
Press through the heels and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the shoulders to the knees, keeping the chin off the chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then lower the spine to the floor one vertebra at a time.

title: Flexion Leg Sit-Up
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor, arms reaching along your sides.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor, arms reaching along your sides.
Draw the navel in toward the spine so the lower back stays in contact with the floor. This is the starting position.
Curl the head, shoulders and upper back off the floor as you breathe out, reaching the hands past the knees.
Lower slowly one vertebra at a time as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Front Toe Touch
summary: Stand tall with the feet together and the knees straight but not locked.
steps: Stand tall with the feet together and the knees straight but not locked.
Let the arms hang and lengthen the spine upward. This is the starting position.
Hinge forward from the hips and reach your hands toward your toes, letting the head hang heavy.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds where the hamstrings feel a steady pull, then bend the knees and roll up slowly.

title: Plyometric Side Lunge Stretch
summary: Stand with the feet wide apart and the toes pointing forward, hands together in front of your chest.
steps: Stand with the feet wide apart and the toes pointing forward, hands together in front of your chest.
Shift your weight onto one leg, bending that knee and pushing the hips back while the other leg stays straight.
Feel the stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg and hold the bottom position for a moment.
Push off the bent leg and spring across to the other side, landing softly in the mirror-image position.
Keep alternating sides for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Single Leg Stretch - Bent Knee
summary: Lie on your back, curl the head and shoulders off the mat and draw one knee in toward your chest.
steps: Lie on your back, curl the head and shoulders off the mat and draw one knee in toward your chest.
Hold the bent knee with both hands and extend the other leg out at about 45 degrees, keeping the lower back pressed down. This is the starting position.
Switch legs in a controlled scissor, drawing the other knee in and extending the first leg out as you breathe out.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then lower the head and both feet to the mat.

title: Single Straight Leg Stretch
summary: Lie on your back with the head and shoulders curled off the mat and both legs straight, one raised toward the ceiling.
steps: Lie on your back with the head and shoulders curled off the mat and both legs straight, one raised toward the ceiling.
Hold the raised leg behind the calf or thigh, keeping both knees straight and the lower back pressed into the mat. This is the starting position.
Pulse the raised leg gently toward you twice, then scissor the legs and repeat with the other leg.
Keep the movement flowing for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then lower both legs under control.

title: Treadmill Running
summary: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. Elevation can be adjusted to change the intensity of the workout.
steps: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. Elevation can be adjusted to change the intensity of the workout.

Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than running outside. A 150 lb person will burn over 450 calories running 8 miles per hour for 30 minutes. Maintain proper posture as you run, and only hold onto the handles when necessary, such as when dismounting or checking your heart rate.
tips: 1. Keep your head up and gaze forward, avoiding looking down at your feet
2. Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce the impact on your joints
3. Ensure the treadmill speed is set at a comfortable level that allows you to maintain good form

title: Band High Fly
summary: Anchor a resistance band above head height behind you and take an end in each hand, stepping forward until the band is under tension.
steps: Anchor a resistance band above head height behind you and take an end in each hand, stepping forward until the band is under tension.
Stand in a split stance with the arms out to the sides at shoulder height and a soft bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Sweep both hands down and together in front of your chest as you breathe out, following an arc rather than pushing straight forward.
Let the bands draw the arms back out to the sides slowly as you breathe in, stopping when you feel the chest stretch, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping
2. Exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position
3. Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your hands together

title: Cable Lying Fly on a Flat Bench
summary: Set a flat bench between two low pulleys and take a handle in each hand before lying back on it.
steps: Set a flat bench between two low pulleys and take a handle in each hand before lying back on it.
Press both handles up over your chest with the arms almost straight and the palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, until the hands are level with your chest and you feel a stretch across it.
Bring the handles back together above your chest along the same arc as you breathe out, and squeeze for a second at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the elbow angle fixed throughout.

title: Standing Cable Crossover Fly
summary: Set both pulleys above head height, take a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance with the arms out to the sides.
steps: Set both pulleys above head height, take a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance with the arms out to the sides.
Lean the torso slightly forward with a soft bend in the elbows and the chest lifted. This is the starting position.
Draw both hands down and together in front of your hips as you breathe out, crossing one wrist slightly over the other at the end.
Let the handles pull the arms back out and up along the same arc as you breathe in, until the chest is stretched.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, alternating which wrist crosses on top.

title: Chest Dip
summary: For this exercise you will need access to parallel bars. To get yourself into the starting position, hold your body at arms length (arms locked) above the bars.
steps: For this exercise you will need access to parallel bars. To get yourself into the starting position, hold your body at arms length (arms locked) above the bars.
While breathing in, lower yourself slowly with your torso leaning forward around 30 degrees or so and your elbows flared out slightly until you feel a slight stretch in the chest.
Once you feel the stretch, use your chest to bring your body back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Remember to squeeze the chest at the top of the movement for a second.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Focus on leaning forward slightly to emphasize the chest muscles rather than the triceps
2. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to keep tension on your muscles
3. Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain

title: Deep Push-Up
summary: Place two low parallettes, or a pair of dumbbells set on their ends, at shoulder width and take a push-up position gripping them.
steps: Place two low parallettes, or a pair of dumbbells set on their ends, at shoulder width and take a push-up position gripping them.
Brace the core and the glutes so the body forms a straight line from the heels to the head. This is the starting position.
Bend the elbows and lower your chest between the handles as you breathe in, going deeper than the floor would allow until the chest stretches.
Press back up to straight arms as you breathe out, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips
2. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down
3. Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury

title: Dumbbell Decline Fly
summary: Set a bench to a decline of about 45 degrees, hook your legs over the pads and lie back holding a dumbbell in each hand.
steps: Set a bench to a decline of about 45 degrees, hook your legs over the pads and lie back holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Press both dumbbells up over your chest with the palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, lowering until the hands are level with your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc as you breathe out, and squeeze for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the elbow angle fixed rather than pressing.
tips: 1. Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them
2. Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints
3. Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms

title: Dumbbell Fly
summary: Lie back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.
steps: Lie back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.
Press the dumbbells up over your chest, then bend the elbows slightly and hold that angle. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, until the upper arms are level with the bench and the chest is stretched.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc as you breathe out, squeezing the chest for a second at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the movement an arc rather than a press.

title: Dumbbell Fly on an Exercise Ball
summary: Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in each hand, then walk your feet forward and lie back until the ball supports your shoulder blades and head.
steps: Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in each hand, then walk your feet forward and lie back until the ball supports your shoulder blades and head.
Lift the hips so the torso is level with the knees, press the dumbbells over your chest with the palms facing each other and bend the elbows slightly. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, keeping the hips high and the ball still.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest as you breathe out, and squeeze for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, stopping if the hips start to drop.

title: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
summary: Set a bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, palms facing each other.
steps: Set a bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, palms facing each other.
Use your thighs to help bring the dumbbells up one at a time to shoulder width, then rotate the wrists so the palms face forward. This is the starting position.
Press both dumbbells up over your upper chest as you breathe out until the arms are almost straight, without banging them together.
Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest as you breathe in, taking about twice as long as the press.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then bring the dumbbells down onto your thighs before standing.
tips: 1. Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms
2. Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press to protect your joints
3. Use a weight that allows for proper form and control

title: Dumbbell Incline Fly
summary: Set a bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
steps: Set a bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
Press both dumbbells up over your upper chest with the palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, until the upper arms are level with your shoulders.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc as you breathe out, and squeeze for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.
tips: 1. Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them
2. Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints
3. Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms

title: Dumbbell Incline Fly on an Exercise Ball
summary: Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in each hand and walk the feet forward only a little, so the ball supports your upper back and you are reclined rather than flat.
steps: Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in each hand and walk the feet forward only a little, so the ball supports your upper back and you are reclined rather than flat.
Press the dumbbells over your upper chest with the palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc as you breathe in, keeping the hips lifted and the ball still.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest as you breathe out, and squeeze the chest for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the head supported throughout.

video.men: exercises/men/Chest/Dumbbell Incline Fly on Exercise Ball.mp4

tips: 1. Keep your back supported on the ball and your hips lowered to maintain a stable position
2. Engage your core to stabilize your body and maintain proper form
3. Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them
