title: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
summary: Lie back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at chest level, palms facing each other in a neutral grip.
steps: Lie back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at chest level, palms facing each other in a neutral grip.
Tuck the elbows in to about 45 degrees from your ribs rather than flaring them out. This is the starting position.
Press both dumbbells straight up over your chest as you breathe out, keeping the palms facing each other the whole way.
Lower them back to chest level under control as you breathe in, feeling the stretch without letting the elbows drop below the bench.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Incline Push-Up
summary: Place your hands on the edge of a bench slightly wider than shoulder width and walk your feet back until the body is straight.
steps: Place your hands on the edge of a bench slightly wider than shoulder width and walk your feet back until the body is straight.
Brace the core and the glutes so there is a straight line from the heels to the head. This is the starting position.
Bend the elbows and lower your chest toward the bench as you breathe in, keeping the elbows at about 45 degrees from your ribs.
Press back up to straight arms as you breathe out, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Chest Press
summary: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest, then sit with your back flat against the pad.
steps: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest, then sit with your back flat against the pad.
Take a handle in each hand with an overhand grip and keep the shoulder blades pulled back. This is the starting position.
Press the handles forward until the arms are straight without locking the elbows, breathing out and keeping the back on the pad.
Let the handles come back slowly until your hands are level with your chest, breathing in and feeling the stretch.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your back and head flat against the backrest to maintain proper form
2. Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement
3. Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return to the starting position

title: Machine Incline Chest Press
summary: Set the seat of an incline press machine so the handles line up with the top of your chest, and sit back against the pad.
steps: Set the seat of an incline press machine so the handles line up with the top of your chest, and sit back against the pad.
Take the handles with a neutral or overhand grip, feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back. This is the starting position.
Press the handles up and forward until the arms are almost straight as you breathe out, keeping the wrists in line with the forearms.
Lower the handles slowly back to the top of your chest as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise
2. Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement
3. Exhale as you press the handles forward and downward, and inhale as you return them to the starting position

title: Machine Lying Chest Press
summary: Lie back on the bench of a lying press machine with the handles level with the middle of your chest.
steps: Lie back on the bench of a lying press machine with the handles level with the middle of your chest.
Take a handle in each hand with an overhand grip, feet flat on the floor and the lower back in its natural arch. This is the starting position.
Press the handles straight up as you breathe out until the arms are almost straight, without locking the elbows.
Lower the handles slowly back to chest level as you breathe in, keeping the elbows under the wrists.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Pec Deck Fly
summary: Set the seat so the handles sit level with your shoulders and sit with your back flat against the pad.
steps: Set the seat so the handles sit level with your shoulders and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Take a handle in each hand with the elbows slightly bent and the upper arms roughly parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Open the arms back out slowly as you breathe in, stopping when the chest is stretched but the shoulders have not rolled forward.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Push-Up
summary: Take a face-down position on the floor with the hands slightly wider than shoulder width and level with your chest.
steps: Take a face-down position on the floor with the hands slightly wider than shoulder width and level with your chest.
Push up onto straight arms and the balls of your feet, bracing the core and the glutes so the body forms a straight line. This is the starting position.
Bend the elbows and lower your chest toward the floor as you breathe in, keeping the elbows at about 45 degrees from your ribs.
Press back up to straight arms as you breathe out, keeping the hips level with the shoulders.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Above-Head Chest Stretch
summary: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides.
steps: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Lift the chest and pull the shoulder blades together. This is the starting position.
Draw the elbows back and slightly up until you feel the stretch across the front of the chest and shoulders.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: 1. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears
2. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles
3. Maintain a straight back and engaged core to ensure proper form and maximize the stretch

title: Behind-the-Back Pec Stretch
summary: Stand tall and clasp your hands together behind your back with the arms straight and the palms facing each other.
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands together behind your back with the arms straight and the palms facing each other.
Roll the shoulders back and down and lift the chest. This is the starting position.
Raise the clasped hands away from your back until you feel a stretch across the chest and the front of the shoulders.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds without leaning forward, then lower the arms and release.

title: Dynamic Chest Stretch
summary: Stand with your hands together, arms extended directly in front of you. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand with your hands together, arms extended directly in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, quickly move your arms back as far as possible and back in again, similar to an exaggerated clapping motion. Repeat 5-10 times, increasing speed as you do so.

title: Kneeling Back Rotation Stretch
summary: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
steps: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Place one hand behind your head with that elbow pointing down toward the supporting arm. This is the starting position.
Rotate the torso to open that elbow up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes, until the chest and mid-back stretch.
Return slowly, repeat for 8 to 10 rotations, then change sides.

title: Standing Reach-Up Back Rotation Stretch
summary: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and the knees soft, arms hanging at your sides.
steps: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and the knees soft, arms hanging at your sides.
Reach one arm up and overhead, lengthening that side of the body. This is the starting position.
Turn the chest toward the raised arm and let it travel back behind you, opening the front of the shoulder and the chest.
Come back to the middle and repeat on the other side, alternating for 8 to 10 reaches each way.

title: Standing Wheel Rollout
summary: Stand with the feet hip width apart, holding an ab wheel by both handles, and hinge forward to set it on the floor in front of your toes.
steps: Stand with the feet hip width apart, holding an ab wheel by both handles, and hinge forward to set it on the floor in front of your toes.
Brace the core hard and tuck the pelvis so the lower back cannot arch. This is the starting position.
Roll the wheel forward, letting the body extend toward the floor only as far as you can keep the lower back flat, and breathe in as you go.
Pull the wheel back toward your feet with the abdominals as you breathe out, and stand back up.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, and stop the set the moment the lower back starts to sag.

title: Triceps Dip
summary: To get into the starting position, hold your body at arm's length with your arms nearly locked above the bars.
steps: To get into the starting position, hold your body at arm's length with your arms nearly locked above the bars.

Now, inhale and slowly lower yourself downward. Your torso should remain upright and your elbows should stay close to your body. This helps to better focus on tricep involvement. Lower yourself until there is a 90 degree angle formed between the upper arm and forearm.
Then, exhale and push your torso back up using your triceps to bring your body back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Wide-Grip Push-Up
summary: Take a push-up position with the hands well outside shoulder width and level with your chest, fingers pointing forward.
steps: Take a push-up position with the hands well outside shoulder width and level with your chest, fingers pointing forward.
Brace the core and the glutes so the body forms a straight line from the heels to the head. This is the starting position.
Bend the elbows and lower your chest toward the floor as you breathe in; the wide hands put more of the work on the chest and less on the triceps.
Press back up to straight arms as you breathe out, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl - Overhand Grip
summary: Sit on the end of a bench holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, and rest your forearms along your thighs with the wrists free beyond the knees.
steps: Sit on the end of a bench holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, and rest your forearms along your thighs with the wrists free beyond the knees.
Let the wrists drop as far as they comfortably go, palms still facing down. This is the starting position.
Keeping the forearms flat on the thighs, lift the backs of the hands toward the ceiling as you breathe out, and hold the top for a second.
Lower the bar slowly back to the stretched position as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Standing Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
summary: Start by standing straight and holding a barbell behind your glutes at arm's length while using a pronated grip (palms will be facing back away from the glutes) and having your hands shoulder width apart from each other.
steps: Start by standing straight and holding a barbell behind your glutes at arm's length while using a pronated grip (palms will be facing back away from the glutes) and having your hands shoulder width apart from each other.
You should be looking straight forward while your feet are shoulder width apart from each other. This is the starting position.
While exhaling, slowly elevate the barbell up by curling your wrist in a semi-circular motion towards the ceiling. Note: Your wrist should be the only body part moving for this exercise.
Hold the contraction for a second and lower the barbell back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
When finished, lower the barbell down to the squat rack or the floor by bending the knees. Tip: It is easiest to either pick it up from a squat rack or have a partner hand it to you.

title: Dumbbell Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
summary: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand behind your glutes at arm's length, palms facing back, feet shoulder width apart.
steps: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand behind your glutes at arm's length, palms facing back, feet shoulder width apart.
Let the dumbbells roll toward your fingers so the wrists extend fully. This is the starting position.
Curl the wrists up toward the ceiling as you breathe out, moving nothing but the hands, and squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back under control as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Over-Bench Reverse Wrist Curl
summary: Start out by placing two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench.
steps: Start out by placing two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.

Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the flat bench. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.
Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

video.men: exercises/men/Forearms/Dumbbell Over Bench Reverse Wrist Curl.mp4

tips: 1. Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement
2. Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells, avoiding any jerking movements
3. Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight

title: Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
summary: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, elbows close to the torso and palms facing each other.
steps: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, elbows close to the torso and palms facing each other.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with the wrists hanging free beyond the knees, thumbs pointing up. This is the starting position.
Keeping the forearms still, bend the wrists so the thumbs travel toward the ceiling as you breathe out, and hold for a second.
Lower the hands slowly to the stretched position as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs throughout the exercise
2. Focus on moving only your wrists; avoid using your arms to lift the weights
3. Choose a weight that allows for proper form and control

title: Side Wrist Pull Stretch
summary: This stretch works best standing. Cross your left arm over the midline of your body and hold the left wrist in your right hand down at the level of your hips. Start the stretch with a bent left arm.
steps: This stretch works best standing. Cross your left arm over the midline of your body and hold the left wrist in your right hand down at the level of your hips. Start the stretch with a bent left arm.
Slowly straighten, pull, and lift it up to shoulder height, as pictured. Feel this stretch originate in your back, not your shoulders, and don't pull too hard on the shoulders joint. Switch sides.
tips: 1. Move your wrist slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain
2. Breathe deeply and steadily as you hold the stretch
3. Focus on relaxing into the stretch to allow your muscles to lengthen fully

title: Wrist Circles
summary: Start by standing straight with your feet being shoulder width apart from each other. Elevate your arms to the side of you until they are fully extended and parallel to the floor at a height that is evenly aligned with your shoulders. Tip: Your torso and arms should form the letter "T: Your palms should be facing down. This is the starting position.
steps: Start by standing straight with your feet being shoulder width apart from each other. Elevate your arms to the side of you until they are fully extended and parallel to the floor at a height that is evenly aligned with your shoulders. Tip: Your torso and arms should form the letter "T: Your palms should be facing down. This is the starting position.

Keeping your entire body stationary except for the wrists, begin to rotate both wrists forward in a circular motion. Tip: Pretend that you are trying to draw circles by using your hands as the brush. Breathe normally as you perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension
summary: Secure one end of a band low on a post and loop the other around one ankle, then face the post and hold it with both hands.
steps: Secure one end of a band low on a post and loop the other around one ankle, then face the post and hold it with both hands.
Hinge forward from the hips until your torso is at about 45 degrees, back flat and the working leg straight. This is the starting position.
Sweep the resisted leg straight back and up as far as it will go without the lower back arching, breathing out and squeezing the glute.
Return the leg slowly to the start against the band as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.
tips: 1. Ensure the resistance band is securely attached to the equipment and your ankle to avoid slipping
2. Exhale as you lift your leg back and inhale as you return to the starting position
3. Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee to protect your knee joint and lower back

title: Band Hip Abduction
summary: Anchor a band around a solid post at ankle height and loop the free end around the ankle furthest from the post.
steps: Anchor a band around a solid post at ankle height and loop the free end around the ankle furthest from the post.
Stand side-on with the feet together, holding the post for balance and the band already under tension. This is the starting position.
Keeping the knee straight and the torso upright, raise the working leg out to the side as far as it will go, breathing out.
Return the leg slowly to the middle against the band as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing sides.

title: Band Hip Adduction
summary: Anchor a band around a solid post at ankle height and loop the free end around the ankle nearest the post.
steps: Anchor a band around a solid post at ankle height and loop the free end around the ankle nearest the post.
Stand side-on and step away until the band pulls that leg out to the side, holding the post for balance. This is the starting position.
Keeping the knee straight, pull the working leg in across the midline of your body against the band as you breathe out.
Let the band draw the leg slowly back out to the side as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing sides.

title: Band Lying Leg Curl
summary: Anchor a band low behind you and lie face down on a mat with the free end looped around one ankle.
steps: Anchor a band low behind you and lie face down on a mat with the free end looped around one ankle.
Move forward until the band is under tension with the leg straight. This is the starting position.
Bend the knee to bring the heel toward your glutes as you breathe out, keeping the hip flat on the mat.
Straighten the leg slowly against the band as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.

title: Band Seated Leg Extension
summary: Sit on a bench or chair and anchor a band low behind you, looping the free end around one ankle.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair and anchor a band low behind you, looping the free end around one ankle.
Sit tall with the knee bent to a right angle and the band under tension. This is the starting position.
Straighten the knee until the leg is horizontal as you breathe out, and squeeze the front of the thigh for a second.
Bend the knee slowly back to the right angle as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.

title: Barbell Front Squat
summary: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the middle of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Exhale as you stand up from the squat and inhale as you lower into the squat
2. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning forward excessively
3. Focus on engaging your quadriceps and glutes throughout the movement

title: Close-Feet Leg Press
summary: Sit in the leg press and place both feet on the middle of the platform with the heels almost touching each other.
steps: Sit in the leg press and place both feet on the middle of the platform with the heels almost touching each other.
Press the platform up, release the safety catches and straighten the legs without locking the knees. This is the starting position.
Bend the knees to lower the platform as you breathe in, until the knees are close to your chest and the lower back stays flat against the pad.
Push the platform back up through the middle of your feet as you breathe out, keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than falling inward.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then re-engage the catches before getting out.

title: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
summary: Stand with the feet well outside shoulder width and the toes turned out to about 45 degrees, holding one dumbbell by the bar with both hands between your legs.
steps: Stand with the feet well outside shoulder width and the toes turned out to about 45 degrees, holding one dumbbell by the bar with both hands between your legs.
Stand tall with the chest up and the arms straight. This is the starting position.
Sit down between your heels by bending the knees and pushing them out over the toes, breathing in and keeping the torso upright.
Drive back up through the heels as you breathe out, squeezing the glutes and the inner thighs at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the dumbbell close to the body throughout.

title: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
summary: Hold a single dumbbell vertically against your chest, cupping the top head with both hands and keeping the elbows tucked in.
steps: Hold a single dumbbell vertically against your chest, cupping the top head with both hands and keeping the elbows tucked in.
Stand with the feet shoulder width apart, the toes turned slightly out and the chest up. This is the starting position.
Squat down by pushing the hips back and bending the knees, breathing in and letting the elbows travel inside the knees at the bottom.
Drive back up through the middle of the feet as you breathe out until the legs are straight.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the dumbbell against the chest so the torso stays upright.
tips: 1. Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward
2. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back
3. Focus on pushing through your heels to engage your glutes and quadriceps effectively

title: Dumbbell Lunge
summary: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.
steps: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: As in the other exercises, do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. Make sure that you keep your front shin perpendicular to the ground.
Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

title: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curl
summary: Lie face down on a flat bench with the hips at its edge and ask a partner to place a dumbbell between your feet, or grip it with the soles.
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with the hips at its edge and ask a partner to place a dumbbell between your feet, or grip it with the soles.
Squeeze the dumbbell between the feet and straighten the legs. This is the starting position.
Bend the knees to curl the dumbbell toward your glutes as you breathe out, keeping the hips pressed into the bench.
Lower the legs slowly back to straight as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions with a light dumbbell you can hold securely.

title: Dumbbell Single-Leg Squat
summary: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with the other foot lifted slightly in front of you.
steps: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with the other foot lifted slightly in front of you.
Stand tall with the chest up and the standing knee soft. This is the starting position.
Push the hips back and bend the standing knee, lowering as far as you can control while keeping the knee tracking over the foot and the free leg off the floor.
Drive back up through the heel as you breathe out until the standing leg is straight.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then change legs — hold a rack with one hand if balance runs out before the muscles do.
tips: 1. Start with a lower weight or no weight to master the form before increasing the resistance
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward
3. Keep your balance by engaging your core and focusing on a fixed point in front of you

title: Dumbbell Squat
summary: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).
steps: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability
2. Align your knees with your toes throughout the movement to prevent straining your knees
3. Lower yourself in a controlled manner to maintain balance and form

title: Machine Horizontal Leg Press
summary: Set the seat of the horizontal leg press so that your knees are bent to roughly a right angle when your feet are on the platform.
steps: Set the seat of the horizontal leg press so that your knees are bent to roughly a right angle when your feet are on the platform.
Sit with your back flat against the pad, feet shoulder width apart in the middle of the platform. This is the starting position.
Press the platform away until the legs are almost straight as you breathe out, without locking the knees.
Let the platform come back slowly as you breathe in, stopping before the lower back rounds off the pad.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Kneeling Leg Curl
summary: Kneel in the machine with one knee on the pad, the other foot on the platform and the roller against the back of the working ankle.
steps: Kneel in the machine with one knee on the pad, the other foot on the platform and the roller against the back of the working ankle.
Rest your forearms on the support and keep the back flat with the working leg straight. This is the starting position.
Curl the heel toward your glutes as you breathe out, keeping the hip pressed against the pad, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Lower the roller slowly back to the straight position as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.
tips: 1. Keep your back straight and avoid arching or rounding your spine
2. Focus on engaging your hamstrings throughout the movement
3. Exhale as you curl your leg up and inhale as you lower it back down

title: Machine Seated Hip Abduction
summary: Sit in the abduction machine with the outside of your thighs against the pads and your back flat on the backrest.
steps: Sit in the abduction machine with the outside of your thighs against the pads and your back flat on the backrest.
Take the handles and start with the knees together or as close as the machine allows. This is the starting position.
Push the knees apart as far as they will comfortably go as you breathe out, and hold the outer hips squeezed for a second.
Bring the knees back together slowly against the resistance as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Sit upright with your back firmly against the backrest to maintain proper posture
2. Focus on squeezing your glutes and outer thighs throughout the movement
3. Perform the movement slowly and avoid using momentum to push the legs outward

title: Machine Seated Hip Adduction
summary: Sit in the adduction machine with the inside of your thighs against the pads and your back flat on the backrest.
steps: Sit in the adduction machine with the inside of your thighs against the pads and your back flat on the backrest.
Take the handles and let the machine open your knees only as wide as is comfortable. This is the starting position.
Squeeze the knees together as you breathe out, and hold the inner thighs contracted for a second.
Let the knees open slowly back to the stretched position as you breathe in, never letting the weight pull you wider than the start, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Machine Standing Hip Extension
summary: Stand in the machine facing the pad and place one foot on the platform, with the working foot or shin against the lever.
steps: Stand in the machine facing the pad and place one foot on the platform, with the working foot or shin against the lever.
Hold the handles, stand tall and brace the core so the lower back does not arch. This is the starting position.
Push the working leg straight back and slightly up as you breathe out, squeezing the glute at the end of the range.
Return the leg slowly to the start as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.

title: Machine Standing Rear Kick
summary: Set the machine so the roller sits behind the working thigh just above the knee, and stand facing the frame holding the handles.
steps: Set the machine so the roller sits behind the working thigh just above the knee, and stand facing the frame holding the handles.
Stand tall on the supporting leg with a slight bend in that knee and the hips square. This is the starting position.
Drive the working knee back and up against the roller as you breathe out, and hold the glute contracted for a second.
Let the roller come forward slowly as you breathe in without letting the lower back arch, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.

title: Rear Decline Bridge
summary: Sit on the floor with the legs straight and the heels on a bench or box, hands on the floor behind your hips.
steps: Sit on the floor with the legs straight and the heels on a bench or box, hands on the floor behind your hips.
Press the shoulders down and away from your ears and squeeze the glutes. This is the starting position.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the shoulders to the heels, breathing out.
Hold the top for two seconds, then lower the hips slowly to the floor as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Sled 45-Degree Wide-Stance Leg Press
summary: Sit in the 45-degree leg press and place your feet high and wide on the platform with the toes turned slightly out.
steps: Sit in the 45-degree leg press and place your feet high and wide on the platform with the toes turned slightly out.
Press the platform up, release the safety catches and straighten the legs without locking the knees. This is the starting position.
Lower the platform slowly as you breathe in, letting the knees travel out over the toes until the thighs approach your chest.
Press back up through the heels as you breathe out, keeping the lower back flat against the pad the whole way.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then re-engage the catches before getting out.

title: Smith Machine Chair Squat
summary: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the bar is loaded, step under it and position it across the back of your shoulders.
steps: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the bar is loaded, step under it and position it across the back of your shoulders.
Take the bar with your hands facing forward, unlock it and lift it off the rack by extending your legs.

Move your feet forward about 18 inches in front of the bar. Position your legs using a shoulder width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Look forward at all times and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper and lower leg breaks 90 degrees.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heels of your feet, extending the knees and returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Adductor Stretch
summary: Stand with the feet much wider than shoulder width and the toes pointing forward.
steps: Stand with the feet much wider than shoulder width and the toes pointing forward.
Place your hands on the thigh of one leg for support. This is the starting position.
Shift your weight onto that leg by bending its knee and pushing the hips back, keeping the other leg straight with the foot flat.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds where the inner thigh of the straight leg stretches, then change sides.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the stretch
2. Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, inhaling deeply through your nose and exhaling through your mouth while holding the stretch
3. Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain

title: All-Fours Quad Stretch
summary: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
steps: Kneel on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Shift your weight onto one arm and the opposite knee. This is the starting position.
Reach back with the free hand, take the ankle of the free leg and draw the heel toward your glutes, keeping the hips level and the lower back flat.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then release and change sides.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch
2. Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine to protect your lower back
3. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles

title: Boat Stretch
summary: Sit on a mat with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands holding behind your thighs.
steps: Sit on a mat with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands holding behind your thighs.
Lean back slightly and lift the chest so the spine stays long. This is the starting position.
Lift both feet off the floor until the shins are parallel with it, balancing on the sitting bones, then straighten the legs if you can keep the back flat.
Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then lower the feet and release.
tips: 1. Engage your core to maintain balance and prevent your lower back from rounding
2. Keep your chest lifted and shoulders relaxed to ensure proper form
3. Breathe deeply and steadily to help maintain the stretch and balance

title: Ceiling Look Stretch
summary: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you, both knees bent to about a right angle.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you, both knees bent to about a right angle.
Tuck the pelvis under so the lower back flattens. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm on the kneeling side overhead, look up toward the ceiling and press the hip of that side forward.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds where the front of the hip and the thigh stretch, then change sides.
tips: 1. Breathe deeply and evenly, inhaling as you lift your torso and exhaling as you return to the starting position
2. Avoid forcing the stretch; only lean back as far as is comfortable without causing pain
3. Use a mat or cushion under your knees for added comfort and support
4. Perform this stretch to enhance flexibility in your spine and relieve tension in your chest and neck

title: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
summary: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
Tuck the pelvis under and press the back hip forward until you feel the front of it lengthen. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm on the kneeling side overhead and side-bend away from that knee, adding a small rotation toward the front leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then change sides.

video.men: exercises/men/Stretching - Mobility/Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch.mp4

tips: 1. Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint
2. Perform the stretch with control to avoid overextending your hip flexors
3. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth

title: Hamstring Stretch
summary: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

title: Hip Circles
summary: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and place your hands on your hips.
steps: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and place your hands on your hips.
Keep the feet flat and the knees soft. This is the starting position.
Circle the hips slowly and widely, letting the pelvis travel forward, to the side, back and around through its full range.
Complete 10 circles in one direction, then 10 in the other.

title: Hip Extension Stretch
summary: Lie on your back with both knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
Draw one knee up toward your chest and hold behind the thigh with both hands. This is the starting position.
Pull that knee gently closer while pressing the other leg down into the floor, so the hip and glute lengthen.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then release and change legs.

title: Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
summary: Lie face down on the floor, with a rope, belt, or band looped around one foot.
steps: Lie face down on the floor, with a rope, belt, or band looped around one foot.

Flex the knee and extend the hip of the leg to be stretched, using both hands to pull on the belt. Your knee and your hip should come off of the floor, creating tension in the hip flexors and quadriceps. Hold the stretch for 10-20 seconds, and repeat on the other leg.

title: Hip Flexor Stretch - Rear Foot Elevated
summary: Kneel on one knee facing away from a bench and rest the top of the rear foot on it, with the front foot flat on the floor.
steps: Kneel on one knee facing away from a bench and rest the top of the rear foot on it, with the front foot flat on the floor.
Tuck the pelvis under so the lower back flattens and lift the chest. This is the starting position.
Press the rear hip forward until the front of that thigh and hip stretch, without letting the lower back arch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then step out carefully and change sides.

title: Standing Knee Raise
summary: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart, holding a wall or a rack if you need the balance.
steps: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart, holding a wall or a rack if you need the balance.
Shift your weight onto one leg and keep that knee soft. This is the starting position.
Draw the other knee up toward your chest and hold it there with both hands, keeping the standing leg straight and the torso upright.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds, then lower the leg and change sides.

title: Lying Quadriceps Stretch
summary: Lie on one side with the bottom arm supporting your head and both legs stacked and straight.
steps: Lie on one side with the bottom arm supporting your head and both legs stacked and straight.
Bend the top knee and take that ankle with the free hand. This is the starting position.
Draw the heel toward your glutes and the knee slightly back, keeping the hips stacked and the lower back flat.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then release and turn over to the other side.
tips: 1. Keep your hips pressed into the floor to maximize the stretch in your quadriceps and avoid straining your lower back
2. Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain
3. If you cannot reach your foot comfortably, use a towel or strap around your ankle to assist with the stretch

title: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
summary: Stand tall with the feet together, holding a wall or a rack with one hand for balance.
steps: Stand tall with the feet together, holding a wall or a rack with one hand for balance.
Shift your weight onto one leg. This is the starting position.
Bend the other knee, take that ankle behind you with the free hand and draw the heel toward your glutes, keeping the knees side by side and the pelvis tucked.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then release and change legs.
tips: 1. Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk
2. Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance
3. Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward

title: Runner's Stretch
summary: Step one foot well forward into a long lunge and place both hands on the floor either side of that foot.
steps: Step one foot well forward into a long lunge and place both hands on the floor either side of that foot.
Keep the back leg straight with the heel pressing back. This is the starting position.
Sink the hips down and forward to stretch the front of the rear hip, then push the hips back and straighten the front leg to move the stretch into its hamstring.
Alternate between the two positions for 20 to 30 seconds, then change legs.

title: Weighted Sissy Squat
summary: Standing upright, with feet at shoulder width and toes raised, use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack and the opposite arm to hold a plate on top of your chest. This is your starting position.
steps: Standing upright, with feet at shoulder width and toes raised, use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack and the opposite arm to hold a plate on top of your chest. This is your starting position.

As you use one arm to hold yourself, bend at the knees and slowly lower your torso toward the ground by bringing your pelvis and knees forward. Inhale as you go down and stop when your upper and lower legs almost create a 90-degree angle. Hold the stretch position for a second.
After your one second hold, use your thigh muscles to bring your torso back up to the starting position. Exhale as you move up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.

title: Sit-Up on a Stability Ball
summary: Sit on a stability ball and walk the feet forward until the ball supports your lower back, knees bent to a right angle and feet flat.
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk the feet forward until the ball supports your lower back, knees bent to a right angle and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly behind your head with the elbows wide. This is the starting position.
Curl the torso up off the ball as you breathe out, lifting the ribs toward the hips.
Lower back over the ball slowly as you breathe in, letting the abdominals lengthen at the bottom.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the ball still throughout.

title: Bent Knee Lying Twist on a Stability Ball
summary: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and rest both calves on a stability ball, knees bent to a right angle.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides in a T and rest both calves on a stability ball, knees bent to a right angle.
Press both shoulder blades into the floor and squeeze the ball lightly between your shins. This is the starting position.
Roll the ball and the knees together to one side as far as you can go without a shoulder leaving the floor, breathing out.
Bring them back to the middle using the side of your waist as you breathe in, then repeat to the other side.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

video.men: exercises/men/Abdominals/Bent knee Lying Twist (On Stability Ball).mp4

tips: 1. Keep your shoulders flat on the floor to maximize the stretch in your spine and obliques
2. Move slowly and with control to avoid straining your back
3. Breathe deeply and steadily, exhaling as you lower your knees to the side and inhaling as you bring them back to the center

title: Chest Lift with Rotation
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands lightly behind your head.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands lightly behind your head.
Draw the navel toward the spine and curl the head and shoulders off the mat. This is the starting position.
Rotate the ribcage to one side as you breathe out, reaching that shoulder toward the opposite knee without pulling on your neck.
Return to the centre, still curled up, as you breathe in, then rotate to the other side.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then lower the head last.
tips: 1. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; use your abdominal muscles to lift and rotate your torso
2. Keep your elbows wide to ensure you are using your core muscles rather than your arms
3. Make sure your lower back remains pressed against the floor throughout the exercise

title: Pilates Corkscrew
summary: Lie on your back with the arms long by your sides, palms down, and both legs extended toward the ceiling with the inner thighs pressed together.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms long by your sides, palms down, and both legs extended toward the ceiling with the inner thighs pressed together.
Anchor the shoulders and press the lower back into the mat. This is the starting position.
Circle both legs to one side, down toward the floor as far as your back can stay flat, then across and back up to vertical.
Repeat the circle in the other direction, so the legs draw a corkscrew above you.
Alternate directions for the prescribed amount of repetitions, keeping the circles small enough that the hips never lift.

title: Floor Crunch
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands crossed over your chest.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor and the hands crossed over your chest.
Press the lower back into the floor and keep a fist's width between your chin and your chest. This is the starting position.
Curl the head, shoulders and upper back off the floor as you breathe out, lifting only until the shoulder blades clear the mat.
Lower back down slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your shoulders
2. Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them
4. Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor to avoid unnecessary strain

title: Crunch with Leg Raise
summary: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and the knees bent, feet off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with the hands lightly behind your head and the knees bent, feet off the floor.
Press the lower back down and curl the head and shoulders up slightly. This is the starting position.
Crunch the ribs toward the hips while at the same time drawing the knees toward the chest, so both ends of the body meet.
Extend the legs away and lower the shoulders slightly as you breathe in, without letting the feet touch the floor.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Avoid using your neck or momentum to lift your shoulders; focus on using your abdominal muscles
2. Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort during the exercise
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and knees, and inhaling as you lower them

title: Crunch with Legs on a Stability Ball
summary: Lie on your back with both calves resting on a stability ball, knees bent to a right angle and hands lightly behind your head.
steps: Lie on your back with both calves resting on a stability ball, knees bent to a right angle and hands lightly behind your head.
Press the lower back into the floor and keep the ball still. This is the starting position.
Curl the head, shoulders and upper back off the floor as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Lower back down slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and support your lower back
2. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your shoulders
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them

title: Crunch with Straight Leg Up
summary: Lie on your back with one leg bent and that foot on the floor, and the other leg extended straight up toward the ceiling.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg bent and that foot on the floor, and the other leg extended straight up toward the ceiling.
Reach both hands toward the raised foot and press the lower back down. This is the starting position.
Curl the head and shoulders off the floor as you breathe out, reaching the fingers toward the raised toes.
Lower slowly as you breathe in without letting the raised leg drift, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing legs.
tips: 1. Avoid using your neck or momentum to lift your shoulders; focus on using your abdominal muscles
2. Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort during the exercise
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them
4. Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor to avoid unnecessary strain

title: Front Plank
summary: Lie face down and set your forearms on the floor with the elbows directly under your shoulders.
steps: Lie face down and set your forearms on the floor with the elbows directly under your shoulders.
Push up onto the forearms and the balls of the feet so the body forms a straight line from the heels to the head. This is the starting position.
Squeeze the glutes and draw the navel in so the hips neither sag nor pike, and breathe steadily.
Hold for 20 to 60 seconds, or until the lower back starts to drop, then lower the knees to finish.

title: Hip Raise Bridge
summary: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor hip width apart and the arms by your sides.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat on the floor hip width apart and the arms by your sides.
Press the lower back gently into the floor and take the weight into your heels. This is the starting position.
Drive through the heels and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the shoulders to the knees, breathing out and squeezing the glutes.
Lower the hips back to the floor slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Pilates Hundred
summary: Lie on your back, draw both knees over your hips with the shins parallel to the floor and curl the head and shoulders up.
steps: Lie on your back, draw both knees over your hips with the shins parallel to the floor and curl the head and shoulders up.
Reach the arms long by your sides a few centimetres off the mat, palms down. This is the starting position.
Extend the legs to about 45 degrees, or keep them bent if the lower back lifts, and pump the arms up and down in small, brisk beats.
Breathe in for five beats and out for five beats, keeping the ribs down and the neck long.
Continue to one hundred beats, then bend the knees in and lower the head to finish.

title: Floor Jackknife
summary: Lie flat on your back with the arms extended overhead and the legs straight.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the arms extended overhead and the legs straight.
Press the lower back into the floor and lift the heels and the hands a few centimetres off the mat. This is the starting position.
Draw both knees toward your chest while curling the torso up and reaching the hands past the knees, breathing out.
Extend the arms and legs back out to the long position as you breathe in, without letting the heels or hands touch down.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Split Jackknife Crunch
summary: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the arms extended overhead on the floor.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the legs straight and the arms extended overhead on the floor.
Press the lower back down and lift both heels slightly off the mat. This is the starting position.
Lift one straight leg while curling the torso up and reaching both hands toward that foot, breathing out.
Lower back to the flat position as you breathe in, then repeat with the other leg.
Keep alternating legs for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Pilates Jackknife
summary: Lie on your back with the arms long by your sides, palms pressing down, and both legs extended toward the ceiling.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms long by your sides, palms pressing down, and both legs extended toward the ceiling.
Draw the ribs down and lengthen the neck. This is the starting position.
Roll the hips off the mat and take the legs overhead, then press them up toward the ceiling so the weight sits on your shoulder blades, never the neck.
Roll the spine back down one vertebra at a time as you breathe in, keeping the legs vertical for as long as you can.
Repeat for 3 to 5 controlled repetitions, and skip the exercise entirely if you have any neck complaint.

title: Leg Raise Hip Lift
summary: Lie flat on your back with the arms by your sides, palms down, and both legs extended straight toward the ceiling.
steps: Lie flat on your back with the arms by your sides, palms down, and both legs extended straight toward the ceiling.
Press the lower back into the floor and the palms into the mat. This is the starting position.
Push the feet straight up so the hips lift a few centimetres off the floor, breathing out and using the abdominals rather than swinging.
Lower the hips back to the floor slowly as you breathe in, keeping the legs vertical throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Lying Hip Lift on a Stability Ball
summary: Lie on your back with both heels on top of a stability ball, legs straight, and the arms by your sides for balance.
steps: Lie on your back with both heels on top of a stability ball, legs straight, and the arms by your sides for balance.
Press the heels into the ball and the arms into the floor. This is the starting position.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the shoulders to the heels, breathing out and squeezing the glutes.
Lower the hips slowly back to the floor as you breathe in, keeping the ball from rolling.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Lying Scissor Kick
summary: To begin, lie down with your back pressed against the floor or on an exercise mat (optional). Your arms should be fully extended to the sides with your palms facing down. Note: The arms should be stationary the entire time.
steps: To begin, lie down with your back pressed against the floor or on an exercise mat (optional). Your arms should be fully extended to the sides with your palms facing down. Note: The arms should be stationary the entire time.
With a slight bend at the knees, lift your legs up so that your heels are about 6 inches off the ground. This is the starting position.
Now lift your left leg up to about a 45 degree angle while your right leg is lowered until the heel is about 2-3 inches from the ground.
Switch movements by raising your right leg up and lowering your left leg. Remember to breathe while performing this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Medicine Ball Wall Sit-Up
summary: Sit about a metre from a solid wall with the knees bent and the feet flat, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
steps: Sit about a metre from a solid wall with the knees bent and the feet flat, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Lower your back to the floor and hold the ball above your chest. This is the starting position.
Sit up fast and throw the ball against the wall as you reach the top, breathing out.
Catch the rebound with both hands and lower back to the floor with the ball under control.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, using a ball light enough to catch cleanly.

title: Reverse Crunch
summary: Lie down on the floor with your legs fully extended and arms to the side of your torso with the palms on the floor. Your arms should be stationary for the entire exercise.
steps: Lie down on the floor with your legs fully extended and arms to the side of your torso with the palms on the floor. Your arms should be stationary for the entire exercise.
Move your legs up so that your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and feet are together and parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
While inhaling, move your legs towards the torso as you roll your pelvis backwards and you raise your hips off the floor. At the end of this movement your knees will be touching your chest.
Hold the contraction for a second and move your legs back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Avoid using momentum to lift your hips; focus on using your abdominal muscles
2. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them back down
3. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor to avoid straining your neck

title: Rotating Push-Up
summary: Take a push-up position with the hands under your shoulders and the body in a straight line from the heels to the head.
steps: Take a push-up position with the hands under your shoulders and the body in a straight line from the heels to the head.
Brace the core and the glutes. This is the starting position.
Lower your chest toward the floor as you breathe in, then press back up to straight arms as you breathe out.
At the top, shift your weight onto one hand, rotate the hips and chest to that side and reach the free arm toward the ceiling into a side plank.
Return the hand to the floor and repeat, alternating the rotation side each repetition.

title: Seated Twist - Straight Arm
summary: Sit tall on a mat with the knees bent and the feet flat, or with the legs crossed if that is more comfortable.
steps: Sit tall on a mat with the knees bent and the feet flat, or with the legs crossed if that is more comfortable.
Reach both arms straight forward at shoulder height with the palms facing each other. This is the starting position.
Rotate the torso to one side, keeping the arms straight and level and the hips facing forward, and pause for a moment at the end.
Return through the middle and rotate to the other side, moving from the ribs rather than throwing the arms.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Side Bend on a Stability Ball
summary: Lie sideways over a stability ball so the ball supports the side of your hip and ribs, legs stacked and braced against a wall or spread for balance.
steps: Lie sideways over a stability ball so the ball supports the side of your hip and ribs, legs stacked and braced against a wall or spread for balance.
Place the hands lightly behind your head with the elbows wide. This is the starting position.
Bend sideways over the ball as you breathe in, letting the top side of the waist lengthen.
Lift the torso up sideways until it is in line with your legs as you breathe out, and hold the squeeze for a second.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then turn over and work the other side.

title: Anchored Sit-Up
summary: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
steps: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Weighted Lying Twist
summary: Lie on your back holding a weight plate or a dumbbell in both hands with the arms pointing straight up over your chest.
steps: Lie on your back holding a weight plate or a dumbbell in both hands with the arms pointing straight up over your chest.
Bend the knees over your hips so the shins are parallel to the floor, and press the lower back down. This is the starting position.
Let the knees travel slowly to one side as far as you can go while both shoulders stay on the floor and the arms stay vertical.
Bring the knees back to the middle using the side of your waist, then repeat to the other side.
Keep alternating for the prescribed amount of repetitions, using a weight light enough to hold the arms still.

title: Band Bent-Over Rear Lateral Raise
summary: Stand on the middle of a resistance band and take an end in each hand, then hinge forward from the hips until your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
steps: Stand on the middle of a resistance band and take an end in each hand, then hinge forward from the hips until your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Let the hands hang under your chest with the elbows slightly bent and the back flat. This is the starting position.
Raise both arms out to the sides until the elbows reach shoulder height as you breathe out, leading with the elbows and keeping the torso still.
Lower the hands back under your chest slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Band One-Arm Front Raise
summary: Stand on one end of a resistance band and hold the other end in the opposite hand, arm straight down in front of your thigh.
steps: Stand on one end of a resistance band and hold the other end in the opposite hand, arm straight down in front of your thigh.
Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and a slight bend in the working elbow. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm straight out in front of you to shoulder height as you breathe out, with the palm facing down and no swing in the torso.
Lower the hand slowly back to your thigh as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing arms.

title: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
summary: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand back from it holding an end in each hand, arms straight out in front of you.
steps: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand back from it holding an end in each hand, arms straight out in front of you.
Stand tall with the feet hip width apart and the band already under tension. This is the starting position.
Pull the hands back toward your chest with the elbows high and wide, so the upper arms travel out to the sides rather than along your ribs.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a second, then let the arms straighten slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band towards your chin and inhaling as you return to the starting position
2. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize rear delt engagement
3. Adjust the band’s resistance by stepping on it closer to or farther from the anchor point

title: Barbell Front Raise
summary: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width, the bar resting against the front of your thighs.
steps: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width, the bar resting against the front of your thighs.
Keep the arms straight with a slight bend at the elbows and brace the core. This is the starting position.
Raise the bar in an arc straight out in front of you until it reaches shoulder height, breathing out and keeping the torso still.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions without swinging.
tips: 1. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on the joints
2. Lift with your shoulders rather than swinging your body to ensure proper muscle engagement
3. Keep your core tight to support your lower back and maintain proper posture

title: Barbell Seated Behind-the-Head Press
summary: Sit on a Military Press Bench with a bar behind your head and either have a spotter give you the bar (better on the rotator cuff this way) or pick it up yourself carefully with a pronated grip (palms facing forward). Tip: Your grip should be wider than shoulder width and it should create a 90-degree angle between the forearm and the upper arm as the barbell goes down.
steps: Sit on a Military Press Bench with a bar behind your head and either have a spotter give you the bar (better on the rotator cuff this way) or pick it up yourself carefully with a pronated grip (palms facing forward). Tip: Your grip should be wider than shoulder width and it should create a 90-degree angle between the forearm and the upper arm as the barbell goes down.

Once you pick up the barbell with the correct grip length, lift the bar up over your head by locking your arms. Hold at about shoulder level and slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Lower the bar down to the collarbone slowly as you inhale.
Lift the bar back up to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Barbell Upright Row - Wide Grip
summary: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip set wider than shoulder width, the bar resting on your thighs.
steps: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip set wider than shoulder width, the bar resting on your thighs.
Keep the back straight, the chest up and a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Lift the bar close to your body up to about chest height as you breathe out, driving with the elbows so they stay higher than the wrists.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs as you breathe in. The wide grip keeps the shoulders in a safer position than a narrow one.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, stopping if the shoulders feel pinched at the top.
tips: 1. Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to avoid leaning forward
2. Lead with your elbows to ensure proper muscle engagement and avoid wrist strain
3. Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell

title: Cable Crossover Reverse Fly
summary: Set both pulleys to shoulder height, stand in the middle and take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left, so the cables cross in front of you.
steps: Set both pulleys to shoulder height, stand in the middle and take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left, so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand tall with the arms out in front at shoulder height and a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Pull the handles apart and back until your arms are out to the sides in line with your shoulders, breathing out and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Let the cables draw the arms back in front of you slowly as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: 1. Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return to the starting position
2. Keep your elbows slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints
3. Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement

title: Cable Front Raise
summary: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley, stand with your back to the stack and hold the bar in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley, stand with your back to the stack and hold the bar in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Step forward until the cable is under tension, stand tall and keep a slight bend in the elbows. This is the starting position.
Raise the bar straight out in front of you to shoulder height as you breathe out, keeping the torso still and the palms facing down.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

title: Cable Lateral Raise
summary: Set a low pulley and stand side-on to it, taking the handle in the hand furthest from the stack so the cable passes in front of your body.
steps: Set a low pulley and stand side-on to it, taking the handle in the hand furthest from the stack so the cable passes in front of your body.
Let the working arm hang across your thighs with a slight bend in the elbow, and hold the frame with the other hand. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm out to the side until the hand reaches shoulder height as you breathe out, leading with the elbow.
Lower the arm slowly back across your body as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing sides.
tips: 1. Choose a weight that allows you to complete the exercise with proper form
2. Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down
3. Avoid using momentum; focus on the contraction of your shoulder muscles

title: Cable One-Arm Front Raise
summary: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, face away from the stack and hold the handle in one hand in front of your thigh, palm facing back.
steps: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, face away from the stack and hold the handle in one hand in front of your thigh, palm facing back.
Stand tall with the feet staggered for balance and a slight bend in the working elbow. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm straight out in front of you until it is slightly above parallel with the floor, breathing out and pausing for a second at the top.
Lower the hand slowly back to your thigh as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing arms.
tips: 1. Avoid locking your elbow; keep a slight bend to reduce strain on your joints
2. Exhale as you raise the handle and inhale as you lower it back down
3. Avoid locking your elbow; keep a slight bend to reduce strain on your joints

title: Cable One-Arm Lateral Raise
summary: Set a single handle on a low pulley and stand side-on to the stack, taking the handle in the far hand so the cable crosses your body.
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley and stand side-on to the stack, taking the handle in the far hand so the cable crosses your body.
Stand tall with the working arm across the front of your thighs and the elbow slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Raise the arm out to the side in one smooth arc until the elbow is level with your shoulder, breathing out and holding for a second.
Lower the arm slowly along the same arc as you breathe in, and repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions before changing sides.

title: Cable Rear Delt Row with a Rope
summary: Sit in the same position on a low pulley row station as you would if you were doing seated cable rows for the back.
steps: Sit in the same position on a low pulley row station as you would if you were doing seated cable rows for the back.
Attach a rope to the pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip. Your arms should be extended and parallel to the floor with the elbows flared out.
Keep your lower back upright and slide your hips back so that your knees are slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Pull the cable attachment towards your upper chest, just below the neck, as you keep your elbows up and out to the sides. Continue this motion as you exhale until the elbows travel slightly behind the back. Tip: Keep your upper arms horizontal, perpendicular to the torso and parallel to the floor throughout the motion.
Go back to the initial position where the arms are extended and the shoulders are stretched forward. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

title: Dumbbell Seated Press with Back Support
summary: Set a bench upright and sit back against it with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, feet flat on the floor.
steps: Set a bench upright and sit back against it with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, feet flat on the floor.
Use your thighs to bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height and turn the palms to face forward, elbows under the wrists. This is the starting position.
Press both dumbbells straight overhead as you breathe out until the arms are almost straight, without letting them clash at the top.
Lower them slowly back to shoulder height as you breathe in, keeping the back against the pad so the lower back does not arch.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then bring the dumbbells down onto your thighs before standing.

title: Dumbbell Front Raise
summary: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells on front of your thighs at arms length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs. This will be your starting position.
steps: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells on front of your thighs at arms length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the left dumbbell to the front with a slight bend on the elbow and the palms of the hands always facing down. Continue to go up until you arm is slightly above parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this portion of the movement and pause for a second at the top. Inhale after the second pause.
Now lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you simultaneously lift the right dumbbell.
Continue alternating in this fashion until all of the recommended amount of repetitions have been performed for each arm.
tips: 1. Avoid swinging the weights; use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells
2. Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce joint strain
3. Keep your shoulders down and relaxed throughout the exercise

title: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
summary: Set a bench to a steep incline of about 60 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
steps: Set a bench to a steep incline of about 60 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
Bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height with the palms facing each other, elbows under the wrists. This is the starting position.
Press both dumbbells straight up until the arms are almost locked out as you breathe out, keeping the palms facing each other the whole way.
Lower them back to shoulder height under control as you breathe in, taking about twice as long as the press.
Repeat for the prescribed amount of repetitions, then bring the dumbbells down onto your thighs before standing.

title: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise
summary: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench.
steps: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench.
